IpaGueuAft.problem: EEG visual decoders align signals with frozen pretrained visual embeddings and treat time uniformly, causing a machine-vision versus human-perception mismatch and ignoring the temporal sparsity of decodable information.
IpaGueuAft.method: BEAT trains a brain-aligned visual encoder with a dual-alignment strategy that combines multi-teacher visual distillation and cross-modal contrastive learning. A lightweight adaptive temporal recalibration module emphasizes informative signal intervals and suppresses noisy ones, and can be attached to various backbones.
IpaGueuAft.key_idea: Train the visual encoder with multi-teacher distillation and EEG-image contrastive loss, and reweight EEG time intervals with a plug-and-play temporal recalibration module.
IpaGueuAft.evidence: Zero-shot brain-to-image retrieval experiments and reconstruction results; datasets and numbers are not given in the abstract.

CGpramjSck.one_liner: Replaces DMD's auxiliary score model with discriminator heads whose logits give log-density ratios for distilling few-step generators.
CGpramjSck.problem: Distribution Matching Distillation must keep an auxiliary diffusion model fitted to the student's evolving distribution, at extra memory and computation cost.
CGpramjSck.method: DMAD recasts distribution matching as classification: two discriminator heads on a shared backbone separate real data and teacher samples from the student's, and linear losses on their logits train the student without auxiliary score fitting. Gap-based reweighting adapts teacher supervision across noise levels using the real-data head's logit gap between real and teacher samples.
CGpramjSck.key_idea: Use discriminator logits as log-density ratios (classical identity) so linear logit losses recover the DMD gradient without fitting an auxiliary score model.
CGpramjSck.evidence: A proof that at the discriminator optimum the losses recover the DMD distribution-matching gradient, plus experiments on ImageNet-64x64, SDXL on COCO-10K, Wan2.1-T2V-14B with VBench, and a human preference study on MiniMax-H3-33B.
CGpramjSck.claimed_gains: FID of 1.04 with one-step generation on ImageNet-64x64, 14.47 with four-step SDXL on COCO-10K, a VBench total score of 85.15 with four-step Wan2.1-T2V-14B, and 79.1% overall human preference on MiniMax-H3-33B (comparison truncated in the abstract).

KdX3ITKCSj.one_liner: Permutation synchronization by exact per-object linear assignment updates, unrolled into a network with learned edge trust.
KdX3ITKCSj.problem: Permutation synchronization solvers that relax the combinatorial problem to a continuous domain lose tightness and must round the solution back.
KdX3ITKCSj.method: CAPS fixes all other objects' assignments, so the objective is exactly affine in the remaining object's assignment and each update is a linear assignment problem with a totally unimodular constraint matrix, solved exactly. CLAPS unrolls CAPS into a lightweight network that learns per-layer constants and a per-edge trust function end-to-end so it can decline outliers.
KdX3ITKCSj.key_idea: Block-coordinate ascent where each object's update is an exact linear assignment problem (the objective is affine in it once others are fixed), with no relaxation or rounding.
KdX3ITKCSj.evidence: Proofs that CAPS increases the objective monotonically, terminates after finitely many passes at a block-wise optimal assignment, and costs time linear in the number of observed matches per pass, plus experiments on SPair-71k and Willow Object.
KdX3ITKCSj.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says CLAPS outperforms the state of the art in precision and F-score on SPair-71k and Willow Object.

eYOSZZ9Fal.one_liner: Shows that longer training contexts shift LLMs from parametric internalization toward reliance on context, hurting beyond an optimum.
eYOSZZ9Fal.problem: Long-context training assumes longer contexts expose richer evidence, but abundant context may reduce the incentive to encode information in parameters.
eYOSZZ9Fal.method: They propose the Information Abundance Paradox hypothesis and test it by varying the context window in pretraining with long documents and the amount of task-relevant train-time context in supervised fine-tuning. They then analyze gradient pressure across feed-forward versus attention modules and run causal interventions.
eYOSZZ9Fal.key_idea: Longer training context offers a lower-complexity path to reduce loss, shifting gradient pressure from feed-forward to attention modules and increasing reliance on context.
eYOSZZ9Fal.evidence: Pretraining with long documents evaluated on language modeling, natural language understanding, and closed-book QA, SFT with varying train-time context, gradient-pressure analysis, and causal interventions.

NGHAx9Mp9R.one_liner: Proves action-blind uncertainty policies have worst-case regret, and introduces FAVE to estimate per-action repair value from logs.
NGHAx9Mp9R.problem: Calibrated uncertainty omits the oriented state-action effect that determines whether an intervention crosses a decision boundary, so equally uncertain questions can need opposite interventions.
NGHAx9Mp9R.method: They prove a tight worst-case regret of Delta(1-1/K) for every action-blind policy over K interventions, characterize identifiable effects under decision-preserving transformations through anchored margins and anchored cycles, and introduce FAVE, which estimates conditional action value by sharing need, response, and direction across actions.
NGHAx9Mp9R.key_idea: Estimate conditional action value by factorizing it into need, response, and direction shared across interventions, because uncertainty alone cannot orient the effect of an action.
NGHAx9Mp9R.evidence: Minimax regret and identifiability theory, plus empirical results on 30,918 natural matching cycles and a 2,000-item, five-intervention portfolio.
NGHAx9Mp9R.claimed_gains: Conditional repair rises from 16.8% to 72.7% after boundary crossing across 30,918 natural matching cycles, and FAVE exceeds equal-information pooled prediction by .0096 (two-way 95% CI [.0030,.0163]) and by .0203 on held-out intervention types.

yLEH2uLAgc.one_liner: An agentic pipeline that decomposes a single image into CAD components, reasons geometrically, and synthesizes CadQuery programs.
yLEH2uLAgc.problem: Recovering editable parametric CAD from a single-view image is hard because geometric observations are incomplete and inter-part relationships are complex.
yLEH2uLAgc.method: CADForge decomposes an object into CAD-meaningful components, identifies CAD-relevant constraints, translates them into modeling parameters through mathematical code, and synthesizes component-wise CadQuery programs. A review agent evaluates the geometry and gives feedback for iterative refinement, while a failure-guided toolkit and a compact parametric CAD memory support robustness and efficiency.
yLEH2uLAgc.key_idea: Infer modeling parameters through explicit constraint-then-math-code geometric reasoning per component, then refine executable CadQuery programs with a review agent's feedback.
yLEH2uLAgc.evidence: Experiments on diverse single- and multi-part objects against existing baselines, measuring reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality; datasets and numbers are not stated.

DM4t0JoJnl.one_liner: Federated multimodal graph learning that decouples semantic and topological tracks and aligns clients by task kernel compatibility.
DM4t0JoJnl.problem: Multimodal graph encoders entangle node semantics with neighbor topology, and task-agnostic alignment forces unrelated tasks onto one manifold, causing negative transfer.
DM4t0JoJnl.method: On the client, Gram-Schmidt semantic-topological decoupling exposes the semantics-orthogonal residual of neighbor context and softly combines it with task-relevant aggregated information, yielding a semantic track and a topology-oriented track. On the server, Task Kernel Alignment estimates label-free public-probe compatibility between clients, followed by personalized dual-track synergistic components whose details are truncated in the abstract.
DM4t0JoJnl.key_idea: Separate the semantics-orthogonal residual of neighbor context via Gram-Schmidt, and align clients according to label-free task-kernel compatibility on public probes.
DM4t0JoJnl.evidence: The abstract is truncated before the experiments; no datasets or results are stated.

i0gZeiXIOC.one_liner: Normalizes GRPO advantages with Pearson correlation coefficients instead of raw reward covariances for multi-reward training.
i0gZeiXIOC.problem: In multi-reward GRPO, correlated rewards with large scales dominate the standard-deviation normalization of the summed reward and suppress signals from smaller-scale rewards.
i0gZeiXIOC.method: CorrGRPO normalizes pairwise covariances into Pearson correlation coefficients, keeping the centered total reward unchanged while balancing the influence of differently scaled rewards in the normalization. Advantage magnitudes still adapt to reward correlations.
i0gZeiXIOC.key_idea: Replace the variance of the summed reward, a sum of pairwise covariances, with a correlation-coefficient-based normalizer so no large-scale reward dominates.
i0gZeiXIOC.evidence: Comparisons against GRPO and other variants on code generation, tool calling, and agent security, using models from 0.5B to 8B parameters.
i0gZeiXIOC.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that results show improvements, and the text is truncated).

Hkx2BnRPC0.one_liner: Adds an auxiliary loss aligning last-layer hidden states of correct rollouts at the anchor token during RLVR.
Hkx2BnRPC0.problem: RLVR reduces each correct rollout to a single reward bit and ignores the geometric structure shared among their hidden states.
Hkx2BnRPC0.method: Hidden-Align is an auxiliary loss that aligns the last-layer hidden states of correct rollouts at the anchor token (the position immediately before the answer marker) during RL training. They observe that correct rollouts already converge there (cosine similarity about 0.84), and full alignment pushes the model toward a unified correct-decision representation.
Hkx2BnRPC0.key_idea: Pull together last-layer hidden states of correct rollouts at the pre-answer anchor token to extract a path-independent correct-decision representation.
Hkx2BnRPC0.evidence: Eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 14B against a DAPO baseline, with pass@k results, other RL algorithms and model families, spatial reasoning, and ablations.
Hkx2BnRPC0.claimed_gains: Average pass@1 over the DAPO baseline improves by 3.8, 6.2, and 5.4 percentage points on Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 14B respectively.

qi0jheYLaZ.one_liner: Allocates adversarial regularization across input directions using complementary damped filters on the representation Jacobian's singular spectrum.
qi0jheYLaZ.problem: Adversarial training applies one ambient geometry to all local input directions, while manifold-aware defenses need a hard tangent-normal decomposition that is unavailable.
qi0jheYLaZ.method: R-CDFR uses complementary damped filters to define a high-gain pass branch and a low-gain residual branch from the singular spectrum of the classifier's representation Jacobian. It combines spectrum-wide inverse-metric slope control, concentrated residual-gradient suppression, and finite-step predictive consistency along pass-filtered perturbations, all computed matrix-free with Jacobian-vector and vector-Jacobian products.
qi0jheYLaZ.key_idea: Split local directions by representation-Jacobian gain with complementary damped filters and regularize the pass and residual branches with separate terms, avoiding a hard partition.
qi0jheYLaZ.evidence: A derived local loss-growth bound, plus experiments across datasets, training recipes, convolutional and transformer backbones, and analytic tasks with known directional geometry.
qi0jheYLaZ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports consistent robustness gains without numbers).

jgikHHDtTV.one_liner: Benchmark of 541 synthetic instances testing whether agents recognize underdetermined personal-memory conflicts and ask clarifying questions.
jgikHHDtTV.problem: Existing memory benchmarks reward designated outcomes and overlook whether agents recognize underdetermination, preserve alternatives, seek missing information, and act in line with the evidence.
jgikHHDtTV.method: TANGLE has 541 fully synthetic instances over 40 personas and three conflict types (Context-Partitioned, Behavior-Oscillation, Source-Contradiction). It evaluates matched oracle (curated memory) and pipeline (system-retrieved memory from multi-session dialogues) tracks.
jgikHHDtTV.key_idea: Score agents on recognizing underdetermined memory conflicts, preserving alternatives, targeted clarification, and calibrated action, rather than on a single designated answer.
jgikHHDtTV.evidence: Evaluation of agents on 541 instances in oracle and pipeline tracks; the abstract reports that explicit conflict recognition is more frequent than calibrated-action or targeted-clarification behavior.

46ccnONDJU.one_liner: Composes a language expert's token prior with a grounding expert's visual likelihood into one teacher for multimodal on-policy distillation.
46ccnONDJU.problem: Using a VLM teacher's full predictive distribution entangles visual grounding with its language prior, while stronger visual supervision can improve perception but degrade language reasoning.
46ccnONDJU.method: Under a generalized Bayesian formulation, the language expert provides a prior over candidate tokens and the grounding expert contributes a visual likelihood that updates it. Adaptive calibration sets how strongly the likelihood updates the prior at each decoding prefix, using the grounding expert's image-induced prediction shift as a prefix-dependent reference.
46ccnONDJU.key_idea: Treat the grounding expert as a visual likelihood that updates the language expert's prior, with per-prefix calibration from the image-induced prediction shift.
46ccnONDJU.evidence: The abstract is truncated before the experiments; no benchmarks or results are stated.

BZCSZkCmKW.one_liner: Localizes critical spans in student trajectories, has a privileged teacher regenerate only those spans, and trains on them.
BZCSZkCmKW.problem: Off-policy context distillation suffers from exposure bias, while on-policy context distillation trains on student rollouts whose states are often uninformative and miss behaviors the student cannot yet produce.
BZCSZkCmKW.method: LoCD first localizes the critical spans of a student trajectory that need revision. The teacher, given privileged information from experience, regenerates only these spans from the student's own prefix, and the student is trained on the regenerated segments.
BZCSZkCmKW.key_idea: The teacher regenerates only the critical spans starting from the student's own prefix, so training targets informative states while exposure bias stays low.
BZCSZkCmKW.evidence: Experiments across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agent tasks against baselines; specific datasets and models are not stated.
BZCSZkCmKW.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports consistent gains over strong baselines, more stable training, and smaller, sparser parameter updates, without numbers).

zV3mnmHXGQ.one_liner: Uses within-scan functional-connectivity re-estimation to weight cross-site alignment for rs-fMRI out-of-distribution generalization.
zV3mnmHXGQ.problem: Cross-site agreement in learned FC representations does not guarantee that predictive evidence stays supported when FC graphs are re-estimated from finite, temporally correlated BOLD sequences.
zV3mnmHXGQ.method: BRIO maps full-scan graphs and their re-estimates into consistently indexed connectome factors and measures re-estimation support from changes in their predictive contributions relative to within-class subject variability and class separation. For each source-site pair and class, this support is combined with predictive relevance into pairwise qualifications that set relative factor weights and overall alignment strength.
zV3mnmHXGQ.key_idea: Weight each connectome factor's cross-site alignment by how stable its predictive contribution is under within-scan FC re-estimation.
zV3mnmHXGQ.evidence: Leave-one-site-out experiments on four real-world datasets (ABIDE, REST-metaMDD, SRPBS, and ABCD) against competitive baselines.
zV3mnmHXGQ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the numbers and says only that BRIO consistently outperforms competitive baselines).

pUyiw6fK2I.one_liner: Gaussian-splatting codec for omnidirectional images using a hierarchical HEALPix primitive grid and rate-distortion-driven primitive pruning.
pUyiw6fK2I.problem: Learned image codecs decode too slowly for immersive VR, while Gaussian-splatting codecs render fast but lag in quality and allocate primitives without considering each primitive's coding cost.
pUyiw6fK2I.method: OIC-GS anchors Gaussian primitives at predefined hierarchical HEALPix spherical locations (no explicit coordinate coding), uses a lightweight entropy model for quantized primitives, and optimizes a spherical rate-distortion objective. Primitives whose quantized opacity becomes zero are removed, so density and level of detail adapt without a fixed primitive budget.
pUyiw6fK2I.key_idea: Fixed hierarchical HEALPix anchors remove coordinate coding, and rate-distortion optimization zeroes the quantized opacity of low-benefit primitives to prune them automatically.
pUyiw6fK2I.evidence: An evaluation on a 100-image set (details truncated in the abstract), with a single bitstream supporting full-sphere, viewport-dependent, and progressive decoding.
pUyiw6fK2I.claimed_gains: The first viewport reaches final quality after decoding only 52% of the bitstream and is then rendered at 1,270 FPS.

11mg8EWICn.one_liner: Closed-loop video world model: predicts an atomic action, generates its clip, then uses the result to choose the next action.
11mg8EWICn.problem: Open-loop video generation cannot adapt to execution outcomes, and existing closed-loop systems rely on pretrained executors or indirect verification, leaving a gap between deciding an action and realizing it.
11mg8EWICn.method: Given an initial image and a task goal, WorldGuide's Planner predicts the next atomic action or task completion from visual progress and its Executor generates the corresponding video clip, both trained on the same step-level procedural demonstrations. Hierarchical visual memory keeps state over long horizons with bounded history token cost.
11mg8EWICn.key_idea: Jointly train a Planner and Executor on the same step-level demonstrations so generated visual states feed back into next-action selection, with hierarchical memory bounding history cost.
11mg8EWICn.evidence: WorldGuide Bench, a set of approximately 59K step-annotated videos built for joint planner-executor training (the abstract is truncated before the results).

c2ZDRVXKfy.one_liner: Proves worst-case lower bounds for heavy-ball, Signum, and Muon that exceed upper bounds of non-momentum methods at common beta.
c2ZDRVXKfy.problem: Momentum's practical speedups are not reflected in smooth non-convex theory, and it is unclear whether unfavorable momentum dependence in existing guarantees reflects loose analyses or genuine worst-case behavior.
c2ZDRVXKfy.method: They compare worst-case bounds beyond asymptotic order, focusing on dependence on the momentum parameter beta. For SHB, Signum, and deterministic Muon they derive lower bounds on averaged gradient norms, and for HB they show a separation under the best-iterate squared gradient norm, each with optimal constant step size.
c2ZDRVXKfy.key_idea: Show lower bounds for momentum methods that exceed the non-momentum upper bounds, so the unfavorable momentum dependence is genuine worst-case behavior rather than loose analysis.
c2ZDRVXKfy.evidence: Theoretical lower-bound constructions in smooth non-convex optimization; no empirical experiments are stated.
c2ZDRVXKfy.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says the gaps widen as beta increases and diverge in deterministic settings as beta approaches one).

50XmWweXjr.one_liner: Predicts a farther point on the same-batch optimization trajectory from two observed transitions, then applies a corrective update.
50XmWweXjr.problem: RLVR repeatedly updates a policy on the same rollout batch, each extra update costs a backward pass, and multi-step methods pay for all intermediate steps.
50XmWweXjr.method: PrePO uses two observed optimizer transitions to estimate a farther point along the same-batch trajectory, moves partway toward it, evaluates the original objective there, and applies a corrective update. Its active cost does not grow with the virtual optimization depth.
50XmWweXjr.key_idea: Extrapolate the optimizer trajectory from two observed transitions, evaluate the objective at the partway point, and correct, giving a fixed cost independent of virtual depth.
50XmWweXjr.evidence: Finite-horizon error bounds for AdamW and Muon and a descent and convergence result for accurate endpoint estimates, plus RLVR experiments and a supervised fine-tuning experiment on a different dataset.
50XmWweXjr.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; PrePO reaches matched performance targets in fewer optimization steps and lower wall-clock time than the corresponding baselines.

HrNjl8x89s.one_liner: Add-on module mapping deployment observations to virtual observations on the original interface for a frozen field reconstructor.
HrNjl8x89s.problem: Amortized field reconstructors trained on a fixed sensing trajectory specialize to its observation interface and degrade under novel or adaptively selected trajectories at deployment.
HrNjl8x89s.method: Trajectory Translator (TT) maps deployment observations to virtual observations on the original observation interface, guiding reconstruction without modifying the frozen reconstructor. Training needs only forward evaluations and input gradients from the frozen reconstructor.
HrNjl8x89s.key_idea: Learn a translator that rewrites deployment observations as virtual observations in the training interface, trained using only the frozen reconstructor's outputs and input gradients.
HrNjl8x89s.evidence: A finite-state Bayesian analysis of when bounded virtual observations preserve evidence exactly, a risk relation for deterministic reconstructors, and experiments on physical-field benchmarks under the evaluated observation-interface shifts.

meVKHN8iFD.one_liner: Training-free block-sparse attention that groups tokens by response and adds a ridge-fitted affine residual correction to sparse outputs.
meVKHN8iFD.problem: In block-sparse attention, queries sharing a block route may attend to different keys, and retaining most attention mass does not necessarily preserve the attention output.
meVKHN8iFD.method: Response-Coupled Partitioning groups key/value tokens by how their keys respond to sampled queries, then groups queries by their responses to key-group centroids. Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction computes exact attention on a few query rows, fits an affine correction to dense-minus-sparse outputs by weighted ridge regression, and adds the predicted residual to each unprobed query.
meVKHN8iFD.key_idea: Partition keys and queries by response for shared sparse routing, then fit an affine map on probed rows to predict the dense-sparse output residual.
meVKHN8iFD.evidence: Relative L2 attention-output error measured across four video generation and world models, compared with semantic block-sparse attention.
meVKHN8iFD.claimed_gains: Attention-output error, averaged over unprobed queries, is reduced by 61.6-90.5% compared with semantic block-sparse attention across four video generation and world models.

zk9NAM53B3.one_liner: Frames tool-agent attack and defense as partially observed state control with DART attacker and SAGE state-querying defender.
zk9NAM53B3.problem: Earlier tool actions can change files, permissions, or records, making a later routine-looking action harmful, yet the visible interaction may not reveal the state needed to judge it.
zk9NAM53B3.method: DART decomposes harmful goals into locally plausible steps and uses feedback from actual tool execution to guide trajectory search, while SAGE investigates relevant state through read-only queries before allowing or blocking each action. They also build an environment-verifiable dataset with controlled initial states, replayable tool environments, and executable checks.
zk9NAM53B3.key_idea: Model attack and defense as control over hidden environment state: the attacker searches with real execution feedback and the defender probes state with read-only queries before each action.
zk9NAM53B3.evidence: Four target models with an environment-verifiable dataset, a recorded-trajectory evaluation of SAGE, and an online attack-defense evaluation (truncated in the abstract).
zk9NAM53B3.claimed_gains: DART improves semantic attack success by 18.8-35.9 percentage points over the competing baseline, and SAGE preserves 95.79% of benign trajectories while intercepting 92.73% of harmful paths.

LJ3qgkXdhV.one_liner: Optimizes discrete per-group option assignments under an exact expected-budget constraint using Riemannian tangent projection and binary-search retraction.
LJ3qgkXdhV.problem: Assigning one of K options to each of N groups under a cost budget has a non-decomposable loss, so combinatorial solvers use proxies, evolutionary search lacks gradients, and penalty methods enforce the budget only approximately.
LJ3qgkXdhV.method: Under softmax relaxation, the budget constraint forms a smooth Riemannian manifold in logit space. RCO wraps tangent projection, binary-search retraction, and momentum transport around an Adam step, combined with Gumbel straight-through estimation and budget-constrained dynamic programming for discrete feasibility.
LJ3qgkXdhV.key_idea: Treat the budget constraint as a Riemannian manifold in logit space with closed-form normal and cost-shift retraction, so Adam steps keep expected cost exactly on budget.
LJ3qgkXdhV.evidence: Geometric properties derived under softmax relaxation (closed-form normal, monotone cost shift, single-inner-product vector transport), with applications named including mixed-precision quantization, non-uniform pruning, and expert selection; the abstract is truncated before results.

mwhmGqUi08.one_liner: Shows Best-of-N utility can recover after an early decline and bounds the labels needed to audit recovery.
mwhmGqUi08.problem: An early decline in Best-of-N utility is often read as a reason to stop scaling N, but it is unclear whether larger N can recover.
mwhmGqUi08.method: They construct a fixed generator-verifier law whose utility peaks at N=2, decreases at N=3, then exceeds the first peak by at least 0.15 at N=H, and explain it through a task-conditional rank transform averaging one calibration profile against a Beta(N,1) density. They then derive minimax audit bounds on label complexity.
mwhmGqUi08.key_idea: Expected Best-of-N utility equals a calibration profile averaged against a Beta(N,1) density, so sign changes of the profile bound the number of utility reversals.
mwhmGqUi08.evidence: Theoretical constructions and minimax audit bounds; no empirical datasets are stated.
mwhmGqUi08.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; for every finite horizon H >= 64 the constructed utility exceeds its first peak by at least 0.15, and passive evaluation needs order-H labels versus a label count independent of H when directly labeling selected winners.

MSAzbHmIuY.one_liner: 3D Gaussian Splatting for HDR novel view synthesis from single-exposure LDR views, using pseudo-HDR supervision and a base-gain representation.
MSAzbHmIuY.problem: Single-exposure LDR views alone underconstrain HDR reconstruction and supervise the camera response function only over a limited range.
MSAzbHmIuY.method: PriorGS guides HDR recovery with pseudo-HDR supervision from 2D single-exposure HDR reconstruction methods, anchored to input LDR views through a closed reconstruction loop, and regularizes the CRF with a learnable prior that guarantees monotonicity. A 3D base-gain representation factors HDR radiance into an LDR base and an overlaid 3D gain field to tolerate cross-view inconsistencies in the pseudo-HDR targets.
MSAzbHmIuY.key_idea: Factor HDR radiance into an LDR base plus a 3D gain field so inconsistent per-view pseudo-HDR targets do not corrupt the Gaussians' color attribute.
MSAzbHmIuY.evidence: The abstract is truncated before the experiments; no datasets or results are stated.

JsY35OC6k7.one_liner: Uses pass@k curves to show high guidance and distribution-matching distillation raise single-sample scores while shrinking coverage.
JsY35OC6k7.problem: Single-draw evaluations such as GenEval2 can hide losses in distribution coverage, so it is unclear whether few-step distilled models truly match their multi-step teachers.
JsY35OC6k7.method: They apply pass@k, the probability that at least one of k independent samples meets a quality criterion, together with CLIP-space analyses linking coverage to within-prompt diversity. They examine classifier-free guidance and few-step distilled models across training objectives.
JsY35OC6k7.key_idea: Plot pass@k as k grows to reveal whether extra samples solve new prompts or only repeat solved ones, exposing coverage that pass@1 hides.
JsY35OC6k7.evidence: pass@k analysis of guidance strength and few-step distilled diffusion models, with CLIP-space diversity analyses; the abstract is truncated before the remaining findings.
JsY35OC6k7.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitatively that higher guidance improves pass@1 but its advantage shrinks and reverses at larger k, and that distribution-matching objectives erode large-budget coverage).

X9BcfhZsuB.one_liner: Consolidates parallel agents' memories and trajectories into evidence-graded shared knowledge for long-horizon exploration on ARC-AGI-3.
X9BcfhZsuB.problem: Parallel exploration generates complementary experience, but shared notes alone do not establish which claims are supported, when they apply, or how conflicting accounts should be reconciled.
X9BcfhZsuB.method: A fresh-context model examines agents' written memories and observer-view trajectories and produces collective entries with supporting evidence, epistemic status, and applicability conditions, which agents query during later exploration. All conditions share a parallel search protocol with level-wise branching, checkpoint handoff, and retries.
X9BcfhZsuB.key_idea: A fresh-context model turns agents' memories and trajectories into collective entries tagged with evidence, epistemic status, and applicability conditions that agents query later.
X9BcfhZsuB.evidence: A comparison of memory treatments under a shared parallel search protocol on the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, with six and nine GPT-5.5 agents and GPT-5.6 Sol.
X9BcfhZsuB.claimed_gains: With six GPT-5.5 agents, RHAE rises from 55.1 to 80.1, completing 22 games and 171 of 183 levels, and nine agents reach 80.9 RHAE and 173 levels.

ZhGlfjgQ2y.one_liner: Post-trains the decoder of latent generative models on generator-produced latents using a Fréchet distributional objective.
ZhGlfjgQ2y.problem: The decoder is trained on reconstruction latents from real images but deployed on generator-produced latents, a train-generation mismatch that FD-based post-training of the generator alone leaves unaddressed.
ZhGlfjgQ2y.method: FDDA freezes the latent generator and directly optimizes the decoder on generation-time latents with an FD objective, for a single epoch.
ZhGlfjgQ2y.key_idea: Fine-tune only the decoder on the frozen generator's own latents with a Fréchet distributional loss, closing the train-generation mismatch.
ZhGlfjgQ2y.evidence: 11 evaluated flow-based and autoregressive latent generative models, measuring gFID, gFDr^6, and wall-clock time, with and without generator-side FD post-training.
ZhGlfjgQ2y.claimed_gains: Across all 11 models, FDDA reduces gFDr^6 by 34.0-59.6% from the pretrained models, gives a further 10.2-57.2% reduction after generator-side FD post-training, and cuts total wall-clock time by 3.6x-328.7x relative to generator-side FD post-training.

XMSwLKtADv.one_liner: Shows that changing only the accumulation order of calibration samples changes Hessian-based PTQ results through floating-point non-associativity.
XMSwLKtADv.problem: Floating-point non-associativity makes the empirical Hessian depend on sample accumulation order, which is usually left uncontrolled in Hessian-based PTQ such as GPTQ.
XMSwLKtADv.method: They vary only the accumulation order of fixed calibration samples across Qwen and Llama models, multiple Hessian-based PTQ methods, and weight bit-widths, and analyze how order-dependent Hessian perturbations are amplified in later Hessian-dependent operations. They also propose numerical stabilization as a practical control, although the abstract is truncated there.
XMSwLKtADv.key_idea: Floating-point order-dependent perturbations in the empirical Hessian are amplified through subsequent Hessian-dependent steps, altering quantization decisions.
XMSwLKtADv.evidence: Controlled order-only experiments on Qwen and Llama models with multiple Hessian-based PTQ methods and weight bit-widths.
XMSwLKtADv.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; order-induced variation is comparable to calibration resampling in some settings, and in some settings exceeds inter-method gaps and reverses method rankings.

DdjjEbh57w.one_liner: An MLLM for instruction-driven segmentation across RGB, multispectral, and SAR imagery, with a variable-channel tokenizer and a 1.9M-sample dataset.
DdjjEbh57w.problem: Existing remote-sensing segmentation MLLMs depend on modality-specific preprocessing or fixed input configurations, and their mask decoders rely on high-level semantic tokens with limited explicit spatial cues.
DdjjEbh57w.method: They curate OmniGlobal-1.9M (1.9 million instruction-segmentation samples from over 800K RS images from 17 sensors and platforms) and propose OmniEarthSeg, with an OmniSensor Tokenizer for variable-channel inputs, a Latent Modality-Aware Modulator, and Prompt-Guided Visual Enhancement that localizes task-relevant evidence before mask decoding.
DdjjEbh57w.key_idea: Tokenize variable-channel multi-sensor inputs into a unified space, modulate by modality, and enhance prompt-relevant visual features before segmentation decoding.
DdjjEbh57w.evidence: Training on OmniGlobal-1.9M spanning RGB, multispectral, and SAR modalities; the abstract is truncated before the experiment details.

Q3dncJ4Sza.one_liner: Quantizes the KV cache of autoregressive video diffusion by predicting keys and values from history and storing low-precision residuals.
Q3dncJ4Sza.problem: The growing KV cache of autoregressive video diffusion costs memory, and LLM-oriented KV quantization transfers poorly to video activations with different statistics and strong spatiotemporal redundancy.
Q3dncJ4Sza.method: TempoKV is training-free: it predicts keys from their temporal history and values from the current key plus a short history of preceding values, then stores only the residuals at low precision. Both predictors are lightweight linear regressions calibrated once offline on a small set of BF16 samples and fixed afterward.
Q3dncJ4Sza.key_idea: Keys are predictable from temporal history and values from the current key plus recent values, so only low-precision prediction residuals are stored.
Q3dncJ4Sza.evidence: Experiments on Self-Forcing, Causal Forcing, and LongCat-Video-13B against existing KV cache quantization methods.
Q3dncJ4Sza.claimed_gains: Higher generation quality than existing KV cache quantization methods at comparable or higher compression ratios, with up to 6.71x KV cache compression.

TNtHw6CKTP.one_liner: A flow-matching VLA that generates action tokens on a non-uniform time schedule and refines low-confidence tokens before execution.
TNtHw6CKTP.problem: Synchronous flow matching uses rigid uniform time schedules without action-context awareness or self-correction, so a single action error can cascade in long-horizon tasks.
TNtHw6CKTP.method: AsyncVLA generates action tokens on a non-uniform schedule with action context awareness, and a confidence rater scores initially generated actions so inaccurate tokens can be refined before execution. A unified training procedure gives one model both synchronous and asynchronous modes, improving KV-cache utilization.
TNtHw6CKTP.key_idea: Asynchronous flow matching over action tokens plus a confidence rater that flags tokens for selective refinement before the action is executed.
TNtHw6CKTP.evidence: Robotic manipulation benchmarks in simulation and real-world evaluations; benchmark names are not stated.

PHFmYhiyde.one_liner: Trains a timestep-free encoder to predict generator states from masked images, then feeds the representation back to guide generation.
PHFmYhiyde.problem: Generator internal states are entangled with noise level and network depth, making stable visual representations hard to obtain from the generator itself.
PHFmYhiyde.method: A separate timestep-free encoder, through a timestep-conditioned predictor, recovers generator states across depths and noise levels from masked clean images, excluding reference noise and masked content from its input. The learned representation then guides the generator, whose updated states supervise further representation learning.
PHFmYhiyde.key_idea: A reciprocal loop: an encoder distills representations predictive of the generator's evolving states, and those representations guide the generator, which in turn supplies new supervision.
PHFmYhiyde.evidence: Frozen linear probing on ImageNet with latent-space SiT and pixel-space JiT in two unconditional settings, without an externally pretrained representation teacher.
PHFmYhiyde.claimed_gains: FID decreases by 19.2-40.8% relative to native training, while linear-probe accuracy improves by 6.80-10.04 percentage points (text truncated).

LdF2t6r72x.one_liner: Splits embodied video generation into world and ego streams using a role-conditioned vision-language predictor and a semantic-routed MoE diffusion generator.
LdF2t6r72x.problem: World prediction relies on visual history and scene stability while ego prediction relies on the current instruction, so a single generation stream entangles them and struggles to keep scene consistency and instruction following in long-horizon navigation-manipulation tasks.
LdF2t6r72x.method: WEM defines the world as the background and unmanipulated objects and the ego as the robot and manipulated objects, and decouples their generation. It combines a vision-language state predictor using role-conditioned attention (RCA) with asymmetric query budgets and a semantic-routed mixture-of-experts (SR-MoE) diffusion generator.
LdF2t6r72x.key_idea: Decompose embodied video into world and ego, predicting each with role-conditioned attention and routing experts semantically in the diffusion generator.
LdF2t6r72x.evidence: HTEWorld, a newly built dataset and benchmark for long-horizon tasks; the abstract is truncated before the results.

y9ufcxjnyi.one_liner: Uses activation patching and probing to show a VLM overwrites readable visual-token labels and answers via different attention heads.
y9ufcxjnyi.problem: Information readable from a VLM's internal states is assumed to be what the model answers from, but this has not been causally tested.
y9ufcxjnyi.method: SightLine changes a value inside the model in a legend-lookup task, verifies the new value with an independent probe, and checks whether the answer follows. They locate eight attention heads through which the answer follows the printed label, and test injecting a row identity at the symbol's tokens to redirect which legend entry is read.
y9ufcxjnyi.key_idea: Install a different label at the symbol's visual tokens, verify it with a probe, and test whether the answer follows, which separates readout from the answering pathway.
y9ufcxjnyi.evidence: Legend-lookup experiments on Qwen models (including Qwen2.5-VL-7B) with the separation replicated in three model families, plus real charts (the abstract is truncated there).
y9ufcxjnyi.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, injecting a row identity switches the answer to the predicted label on 68% and 88% of evaluation pairs in two layouts, while a probe reads the assigned label with perfect accuracy.

SAuycm49Dr.one_liner: Learns a residual correction to initial noise with Local GRPO so a frozen few-step generator improves reward in one pass.
SAuycm49Dr.problem: Reward alignment framed over stochastic trajectories suits few-step deterministic generators poorly, and existing gradient-free initial-noise optimization needs costly per-sample search at inference.
SAuycm49Dr.method: LeNO learns an anchor-conditioned distribution over noise corrections (a learned residual transport) using Local GRPO and scalar rewards while the generator stays frozen, regularized by a derived KL upper bound for Gaussian noise with norm-preserving projection.
SAuycm49Dr.key_idea: Amortize reward-guided initial-noise optimization into a learned anchor-conditioned residual transport trained with Local GRPO, regularized by a KL upper bound to the Gaussian prior.
SAuycm49Dr.evidence: Few-step text-to-image generation and protein structure generation, including expensive black-box designability rewards.
SAuycm49Dr.claimed_gains: Improves target rewards with a single noise correction at inference while largely preserving generation quality and diversity; no numbers are stated.

CtC4OdBY8O.one_liner: Matching upper and lower VC-dimension bounds for gated lookup injection in hard-attention Transformers, in terms of a depth-weighted budget.
CtC4OdBY8O.problem: Lookup modules such as per-layer embeddings and n-gram tables are reported as nearly free in compute, but it is unclear whether each lookup parameter adds less to sample complexity than an ordinary weight.
CtC4OdBY8O.method: They define gated lookup injection (GLI), weight each parameter by the number of layers remaining after its first use to form a depth-weighted budget, prove a VC upper bound, and build a network with a matching lower bound.
CtC4OdBY8O.key_idea: Weight each parameter by the layers remaining after its first use; VC dimension is at most this budget times a log factor, matched by a lookup-only construction.
CtC4OdBY8O.evidence: Theoretical results in the hard-attention Transformer model: a VC upper bound and a matching lower bound that holds whenever context length is polynomial in the budget.
CtC4OdBY8O.claimed_gains: Lookup parameters are as expensive per parameter as ordinary ones, and with b-bit floating-point arithmetic the lower bound gives Theta(b) bits of capacity per table entry.

3tZGsfqG0F.one_liner: Replaces iterative bundle adjustment with a single forward pass of a graph network over cameras, 3D points and observations.
3tZGsfqG0F.problem: Classical per-scene iterative bundle adjustment needs costly optimization, while geometric foundation model outputs are not fully consistent with multi-view tracks.
3tZGsfqG0F.method: Given initial cameras and geometry from a geometric foundation model and fixed multi-view tracks, FFBA builds a sparse heterogeneous graph of cameras, 3D points and 2D observations and refines poses, focal lengths and 3D points with a geometry-conditioned graph network. Uncertainty-guided confidence estimation filters unreliable observations, and a confidence-weighted reprojection loss trains it end-to-end on over 0.9M samples from seven datasets and three foundation models.
3tZGsfqG0F.key_idea: Learn bundle-adjustment update rules shared across scenes as message passing on a camera-point-observation graph, with uncertainty-guided filtering of unreliable observations.
3tZGsfqG0F.evidence: Three in-domain and four cross-domain datasets, comparing against geometric foundation model initializations, classical BA and EPO.
3tZGsfqG0F.claimed_gains: Reduces optimization time by more than an order of magnitude relative to classical BA while improving reprojection consistency and camera accuracy over foundation-model initializations; no other figures are stated.

6NIBXbnSvH.one_liner: OS-like runtime schedules asynchronous Planner, acting and monitoring threads above an 8B navigation VLA, enabling continuous motion and interruption.
6NIBXbnSvH.problem: Language-model planners reason well but physical interaction needs dense, low-latency action policies, so the two must be connected so the robot keeps moving while reasoning and reacts to sudden real-world events.
6NIBXbnSvH.method: A harness runs reasoning, acting and monitoring as asynchronous threads with their own context, tools and permissions, and the runtime decides which thread controls motion, supporting interruption and thread switching. Beneath it, the NavGPT VLA action policy, trained on 19.28M examples, allocates visual tokens by codec allocation in proportion to scene change.
6NIBXbnSvH.key_idea: Schedule asynchronous planner, acting and monitoring threads with an OS-like runtime over a navigation VLA that allocates visual tokens in proportion to scene change.
6NIBXbnSvH.evidence: Vision-and-language navigation benchmarks R2R-CE and RxR-CE, with a comparison against human followers on RxR-CE.
6NIBXbnSvH.claimed_gains: The 8B NavGPT VLA alone reaches 76.94 SR on R2R-CE and 82.39 SR on RxR-CE, and the full harness reaches 81.51 SR on R2R-CE and 90.43 SR on RxR-CE versus 90.4 for human followers, at 1 min 22 s per episode versus roughly 3 min for a human.

ehW2Rqzfcc.one_liner: Coupled world-action predictor adds next-frame feature prediction to trajectory supervision for embodied navigation, sampling only the policy at deployment.
ehW2Rqzfcc.problem: Action labels supervise only low-dimensional trajectories and do not constrain the richer visual changes along a navigation route.
ehW2Rqzfcc.method: A vision-language model integrates the task with long-horizon visual history to condition a shared dual-stream predictor that supports trajectory prediction (Policy) and next-frame feature prediction (NF), with shared parameters and cross-stream attention so NF supervision updates navigation components. Video-instruction pairs without trajectories add NF targets, and target-domain videos support offline adaptation while source trajectories are replayed for Policy supervision.
ehW2Rqzfcc.key_idea: A dual-stream predictor with shared parameters and cross-stream attention lets next-frame feature prediction supervise the same components that output navigation trajectories.
ehW2Rqzfcc.evidence: Continuous navigation benchmarks for vision-and-language and point-goal navigation with separately trained models, and matched data and optimization budget comparisons on RxR-CE.
ehW2Rqzfcc.claimed_gains: Under matched data and optimization budgets, NF improves RxR-CE SR/SPL by 1.5/2.2 points (abstract truncated).

r406Tukywm.one_liner: Represents hyperbolic PDE solutions as a tree of local patches advanced by a small scale-equivariant network using dimensionless scale normalization.
r406Tukywm.problem: Whole-frame neural solvers for hyperbolic PDEs see the entire domain yet yield higher errors, and handling multiple resolutions adds structural complexity to the network.
r406Tukywm.method: PARA stores the solution as a tree of independent local patches at varying resolutions (TreeGrid) and predicts each patch's next state concurrently with a lightweight network from its stencil. Scale normalization uses the scaling symmetry of the Euler equations to make the solver scale-equivariant by construction, and a MultiGrid expansion advances all levels in one batched tensor operation.
r406Tukywm.key_idea: Restrict the network to each patch's stencil, matching the physical domain of dependence, and use Euler scaling symmetry for dimensionless scale normalization.
r406Tukywm.evidence: The gamma = 1.4 subset of the Well's compressible Euler benchmark, compared with whole-frame single-resolution neural baselines.

XFCvcjrkPw.one_liner: Pareto Flow Learning supervises a neural model with ODE residuals of preference-conditioned Pareto gradient flows, meta-learned for multiobjective Bayesian optimization.
XFCvcjrkPw.problem: Existing Pareto set learning methods model task-specific Pareto sets whose terminal solution manifolds can be geometrically misaligned across related tasks, hindering transferable shared structure.
XFCvcjrkPw.method: PFL formulates each preference-conditioned scalarized problem as a continuous-time Pareto gradient flow and trains a network to approximate the flows through ODE residual supervision, so it learns optimization dynamics as well as solutions. A meta version (mPFM) learns shared structure across source-task flows and adapts to unseen targets, and mPFM-MOBO plugs it into multiobjective Bayesian optimization.
XFCvcjrkPw.key_idea: Supervise a network with the ODE residual of preference-conditioned Pareto gradient flows so it captures optimization dynamics, then meta-learn across source tasks.
XFCvcjrkPw.evidence: Experiments on synthetic benchmarks and engineering design problems, including under distribution shift, with ablations on the ODE supervision.

j1kInfIGjy.one_liner: TPL jointly trains a shared actor and critic over several temporal reward weightings to improve the standard discounted policy.
j1kInfIGjy.problem: Standard RL trains with a single fixed discount factor that weights future rewards exponentially less, so the policy gets no benefit from learning under other temporal weightings of the same rewards.
j1kInfIGjy.method: Temporal Perspective Learning (TPL) is an off-policy actor-critic framework that jointly learns perspective-specific policies under different temporal weightings and evaluates the consequences of following each, using a shared actor and shared critic conditioned on the perspective. The shared architecture lets learning across perspectives influence the policy for the standard discounted objective.
j1kInfIGjy.key_idea: Condition a shared actor and critic on a temporal-weighting perspective, learning a separate policy per perspective and evaluating each, rather than decomposing one policy's value across horizons.
j1kInfIGjy.evidence: Experiments on 24 continuous-control tasks across three benchmark suites, with ablations on jointly learning perspective-specific policies and values.
j1kInfIGjy.claimed_gains: Improved performance over the evaluated baselines on 24 continuous-control tasks across three benchmark suites; no effect sizes are stated.

ESUfjmahnd.one_liner: Cold-start recommendation reframed as item-centric multi-user generation using permutation-invariant masked discrete diffusion.
ESUfjmahnd.problem: User-centric recommenders fail in cold start, where sparse feedback prevents reliable representation learning and initial exposure for new items.
ESUfjmahnd.method: PD^2 uses a permutation-invariant Masked Discrete Diffusion mechanism to map item content directly to the latent user space without autoregressive constraints, with Interval-Aware Spatio-Temporal Encoding adding temporal biasing to positional encoding.
ESUfjmahnd.key_idea: Generate a set of seed users for an item in parallel with masked discrete diffusion rather than predicting the next item for each user.
ESUfjmahnd.evidence: not stated; the visible abstract is cut off before the experiments.

M0yUyqrDka.one_liner: Snapshot-free engine that syncs RL policy weights by inverting AdamW updates and sending only changed BF16 elements across heterogeneous layouts.
M0yUyqrDka.problem: Online agentic RL with separate training and rollout services makes frequent policy-weight synchronization a systems overhead, and checkpoint-based sparse sync retains old models and materializes complete intermediates.
M0yUyqrDka.method: AReaL-DTE reconstructs overwritten weights on demand by inverting AdamW updates, streams reconstructed and current parameters through converter-aligned BF16 change detection, and remaps changed elements directly into receiver-local coordinates. It transfers sparsely via shared storage across clusters and a deadlock-safe two-round protocol within a cluster.
M0yUyqrDka.key_idea: Invert AdamW updates to recover the previous weights on demand, detect changed BF16 elements, and remap them directly into receiver shard coordinates without snapshots.
M0yUyqrDka.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B across four online RL workloads (the abstract is cut off after that).
M0yUyqrDka.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before results; it reports that fewer than 2% of BF16 weight elements change between consecutive policy versions)

pymL11fMwT.one_liner: World action model where 32 latent bridge queries link video and action experts, allowing a two-layer action expert.
pymL11fMwT.problem: Dense layer-wise Mixture-of-Transformers attention in world action models exposes action prediction to irrelevant visual features and forces matched expert depths, adding redundant computation.
pymL11fMwT.method: Bridge-of-Experts aggregates visual, language and proprioceptive priors through 32 Latent Bridge Queries into a shared limited latent space. Joint video-action supervision lets action gradients shape the Video Expert, the Action Expert retrieves task-relevant information by cross-attention, and the queries are reused during action denoising.
pymL11fMwT.key_idea: Replace dense layer-wise cross-expert attention with a small set of latent bridge queries, decoupling video and action expert depths.
pymL11fMwT.evidence: LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus simulation, simulation FLOPs profiling and real-robot latency against Fast-WAM, plus ablations.
pymL11fMwT.claimed_gains: 98.25% success on LIBERO and 72.24% pooled success on LIBERO-Plus with a 5.06B model; 28.72% fewer single-sample inference FLOPs than Fast-WAM in simulation and 77.1 ms real-robot latency (2.47x speedup).

XJpRXsXHPz.one_liner: Agentic RL with multi-level process rewards grounded in Lean4-formalized workflows, trained with workflow-stage-normalized GRPO.
XJpRXsXHPz.problem: Agentic RL for software engineering and terminal tasks mostly relies on outcome rewards, with little consideration of low-level tool-call and mid-level workflow-stage rewards.
XJpRXsXHPz.method: Builds a problem-specific workflow system, then formalizes workflows and annotates multi-level rewards in a unified Lean4 schema so agent behavior can be verified within a general harness. The multi-level rewards drive a workflow-stage-normalized GRPO used to train LAR-9B and LAR-27B.
XJpRXsXHPz.key_idea: Formalize agent workflows in Lean4 to verify tool-call and workflow-stage steps, and feed the verified step rewards into a workflow-stage-normalized GRPO.
XJpRXsXHPz.evidence: LAR-9B and LAR-27B compared against the leading model of similar size on software-engineering and terminal-usage tasks (details truncated).
XJpRXsXHPz.claimed_gains: Outperforms the leading model of similar size; LAR-27B achieves 77.3% on a benchmark named in the truncated abstract.

9I3CveOgh3.one_liner: Separate LoRA experts for denoising segments split so each gets comparable cumulative gradient magnitude, for diffusion reward fine-tuning.
9I3CveOgh3.problem: Reward fine-tuning gradients concentrate on certain denoising timesteps, including in direct-gradient optimization, biasing a single shared LoRA adapter toward particular timestep regimes.
9I3CveOgh3.method: GTP-LoRA partitions the denoising trajectory into contiguous segments and assigns one LoRA expert to each. Boundaries come from a reference denoiser-output gradient profile so each expert receives a comparable cumulative upstream gradient magnitude.
9I3CveOgh3.key_idea: Place segment boundaries by equalizing cumulative gradient magnitude from a reference profile, and confine each segment's updates to its own LoRA expert.
9I3CveOgh3.evidence: Experiments across multiple diffusion models, reward objectives, and optimization algorithms.
9I3CveOgh3.claimed_gains: Consistently improves reward performance while maintaining competitive sample diversity; no numbers are stated in the provided abstract.

kA7hGNWP9H.one_liner: Spatio-temporal identity encoder compresses reference videos into identity tokens that condition a frozen audio-driven video diffusion transformer.
kA7hGNWP9H.problem: Appearance-based personalization from reference images misses a person's characteristic behavior, such as head movements while speaking or listening.
kA7hGNWP9H.method: A spatio-temporal identity encoder aggregates a variable number of reference videos into a fixed number of identity tokens that condition a frozen audio-driven video diffusion transformer through dedicated cross-attention layers. A three-stage schedule adapts the encoder to talking-head videos self-supervised, conditions on the target clip as reference, then switches to different clips of the same subject.
kA7hGNWP9H.key_idea: Fixed-size identity tokens distilled from variable reference videos inject appearance and behavior into a frozen audio-driven generator through added cross-attention layers.
kA7hGNWP9H.evidence: Qualitative and quantitative comparison against an appearance-only baseline; datasets are not stated in the abstract.
kA7hGNWP9H.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports more authentic, person-specific videos than an appearance-only baseline without numbers.

K3Yh3jw2FF.one_liner: MLLM latent spatial reasoning: geometry-infused visual tokens form a latent mental map, then reasoning retrieves spatial evidence in latent space.
K3Yh3jw2FF.problem: MLLMs' language-centric representations limit spatial reasoning; geometry injection or textual chain-of-thought keeps reasoning in a language-oriented space, and visual representations can conflate similar objects at different locations.
K3Yh3jw2FF.method: Mental Map Imaging (MMI) internalizes geometric structure into visual token representations to build a latent mental map. Visual-Cue Latent Reasoning (VCLR) autoregressively retrieves question-relevant spatial evidence from that map and reasons with variable length in the spatial latent space.
K3Yh3jw2FF.key_idea: Builds geometry-aware visual tokens as a latent mental map and reasons autoregressively over retrieved spatial evidence in latent space rather than in text.
K3Yh3jw2FF.evidence: The abstract is cut off before the experiments, so benchmarks and baselines are not visible.

qA7EnMZp4z.one_liner: VLA-GSE initializes PEFT experts from spectral decomposition of the frozen VLA backbone: leading components shared, residual components routed.
qA7EnMZp4z.problem: Full fine-tuning of VLA models overfits and forgets pretrained vision-language capability, while existing PEFT methods adapt poorly to robot control.
qA7EnMZp4z.method: VLA-GSE spectrally decomposes the frozen backbone, assigning leading singular components to generalized (shared) experts and disjoint residual components to specialized (routed) experts. This raises adaptation capacity under a fixed trainable-parameter budget.
qA7EnMZp4z.key_idea: Initialize shared experts from the leading singular components and routed experts from disjoint residual components of the frozen backbone weights.
qA7EnMZp4z.evidence: Comparable-budget comparisons with full fine-tuning and PEFT baselines, LIBERO-Plus zero-shot success, multimodal understanding benchmarks against LoRA, and real-world manipulation (abstract cut off).
qA7EnMZp4z.claimed_gains: Updates only 2.51% of full model parameters and reaches 81.2% average zero-shot success on LIBERO-Plus while preserving pretrained VLM capability comparably to LoRA.

uPstvqOoai.one_liner: Uses the target LLM's quantized counterpart as the hybrid-reasoning reasoner, with a shared KV cache and a quantization-error routing signal.
uPstvqOoai.problem: Hybrid reasoning methods need an extra reasoner model and KV cache, raising memory use, and the capability gap between reasoner and target LLM limits speedup or accuracy.
uPstvqOoai.method: ORQA replaces the separate reasoner with a quantized counterpart of the target LLM and a shared KV cache pool. Weight infusion integrates parameters between the target and the reasoner to remove separate model storage while keeping inference lossless, and Quant-ifier predicts token disagreement from the quantization error distribution to route tokens.
uPstvqOoai.key_idea: Fuse full-precision and quantized weights into one stored model, and route tokens to the quantized reasoner using a signal that predicts disagreement from quantization error.
uPstvqOoai.evidence: Experiments compare speed and accuracy against prior hybrid reasoning methods; specific models and benchmarks are not stated in the abstract.

6087HCVTOE.one_liner: VEM keeps every observation as its encoded video latent in context, so a world-action model reads one history-conditioned latent.
6087HCVTOE.problem: World-action models act from a bounded window of recent observations, which makes their decisions effectively Markovian.
6087HCVTOE.method: Verbatim episode memory keeps every demonstration and execution observation in context as its encoded video latent, with no compression, selection or eviction after temporal sampling and VAE encoding. The video expert integrates causal history into the current latent and the action expert reads only this fixed-size state; training uses expert actions and future video targets without memory annotations.
6087HCVTOE.key_idea: Place demonstration and execution history on one uncompressed latent stream so the video expert folds history into the current latent that the action expert reads.
6087HCVTOE.evidence: RoboMME across 16 tasks, an Imitation Suite, and a retrieval test with irrelevant history longer than twice the longest training episode.
6087HCVTOE.claimed_gains: 62.5% average success rate across 16 tasks on RoboMME and 78.2% on the Imitation Suite, versus 49.5% for the backbone with ground-truth subgoals and 64.0% for a language-conditioned VLA.

P5oAeWZ1uu.one_liner: Hierarchical Transformer pretrains city representations via nested attention over entities, blocks, regions, and cities.
P5oAeWZ1uu.problem: Scaling urban representation pretraining across thousands of cities requires modeling local functional interactions within blocks and spatial organization within and across regions.
P5oAeWZ1uu.method: An Urban Fabric Tokenizer converts heterogeneous geospatial data into entity tokens in a unified tensor that mirrors the city hierarchy. The Urban Interaction Transformer then applies attention in three nested stages: entities within blocks, blocks within regions, and regions at city scale.
P5oAeWZ1uu.key_idea: Three nested attention stages (entity-within-block, block-within-region, region-within-city) over a tokenized entity-block-region-city hierarchy, so urban semantics emerge progressively.
P5oAeWZ1uu.evidence: Pretrained on a U.S. geospatial dataset of 8.18 million blocks and over 263 million entities, then evaluated on a multilevel benchmark against strong baselines including Google DeepMind's AlphaEarth.
P5oAeWZ1uu.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says it outperforms strong baselines including AlphaEarth on the multilevel benchmark, with no numeric margins).

pMH2TPrjT9.one_liner: Continuous-time medical treatment RL benchmark built from clinical data with physics-informed neural networks.
pMH2TPrjT9.problem: Existing RL formulations and simulators for treatment are discrete-time MDPs with fixed decision intervals, so they cannot test handling of continuous-time progression, irregular intervention timing, personalization, and safety between measurements.
pMH2TPrjT9.method: MedGym models longitudinal patient evolution in a continuous-time framework constructed from clinical data using physics-informed neural networks. It allows fixed-interval discrete-time and time-adaptive continuous-time decision making to be compared in one environment.
pMH2TPrjT9.key_idea: Define the RL environment as continuous-time patient dynamics fitted to clinical data with physics-informed neural networks, so interventions can occur at irregular times.
pMH2TPrjT9.evidence: A configurable benchmark environment supporting evaluation of personalization and trajectory-level safety; the specific datasets and RL baselines are not visible in the abstract text provided.

kTcYlL22zi.one_liner: Cross-modal point-image pretraining that aligns neighborhood-average and residual features at intermediate encoder stages with image features.
kTcYlL22zi.problem: Point-image alignment on pooled descriptors lets different local feature patterns produce the same descriptor and receive the same alignment signal.
kTcYlL22zi.method: At selected encoder stages, computes neighborhood averages and residuals before pooling and aligns their branch descriptors with image features. Branch-level objectives align each representation with its visual target, while cross-level consistency and adaptive fusion coordinate the branches, over an interface that supports graph encoders and point Transformers.
kTcYlL22zi.key_idea: Supervise intermediate point features through neighborhood-average and residual branches aligned to image features before pooling, rather than only the pooled descriptor.
kTcYlL22zi.evidence: Evaluated on object classification, few-shot adaptation, dense prediction, and low-label scene learning, with same-backbone comparisons and capacity- and computation-matched controls.

eXgqpaDkSp.one_liner: Adversarial merchant interactions test shopping-agent purchase safety, with tool-grounded correction and reinforcement learning mitigating unsafe decisions.
eXgqpaDkSp.problem: Existing e-commerce benchmarks emphasize task completion in benign environments and do not adequately test purchases under deceptive merchants.
eXgqpaDkSp.method: SafeShopBench evaluates shopping agents against deceptive merchant evidence and dialogue. Mitigations include a tool-grounded Detector-Corrector wrapper and supervised fine-tuning followed by outcome-based reinforcement learning.
eXgqpaDkSp.key_idea: Evaluate purchase decisions under deceptive merchant interactions, then revisit decisions with tool-grounded correction or optimize purchase outcomes through reinforcement learning.
eXgqpaDkSp.evidence: Full-tool evaluations cover twelve buyer agents, including Claude Opus 5, and test reinforcement learning on a smaller buyer agent.
eXgqpaDkSp.claimed_gains: Unsafe-purchase rates range from 14.3% to 51.8%, while reinforcement learning reduces the smaller buyer's rate from 24.9% after supervised fine-tuning to 8.3%.

xLUhlfoeKH.one_liner: Solver-certified visual edits and activation interventions test whether reinforcement learning improves evidence-grounded answers in vision-language models.
xLUhlfoeKH.problem: Accuracy gains after reinforcement learning do not establish whether vision-language models use visual evidence rather than language priors.
xLUhlfoeKH.method: CARVE changes individual pieces of visual evidence, certifies the resulting answers, and records the edited regions. It tests numeral changes, label relocation, and whether edited-region hidden states redirect answers.
xLUhlfoeKH.key_idea: Pair solver-certified visual counterfactuals with edited-region hidden-state interventions to separate answer changes from causal use of visual evidence.
xLUhlfoeKH.evidence: Experiments evaluate four Qwen-VL backbones trained with GRPO, VPPO, and PRPO across 16 configurations, including frozen-vision-tower tests.
xLUhlfoeKH.claimed_gains: Models retain original answers after 10.9–39.5% of label moves versus at most 1.7% of numeral edits, while edited regions reproduce 43% of gains in 3B models (95% CI [18, 67]) and 96% in 7B models ([66, 139]).

f1FL6lcnDV.one_liner: Equivariant flow matching combines local geometry, global ring interactions, and chirality supervision to generate cyclic-peptide conformers.
f1FL6lcnDV.problem: Cyclic-peptide ensemble generation must capture long-range ring coupling while preserving local geometry and stereochemistry.
f1FL6lcnDV.method: CycPepFlow generates all-atom Cartesian conformers from molecular graphs using SO(3)-equivariant local interactions and gated global attention. Chirality conditioning and signed-volume supervision preserve stereochemistry, with optional graph-geodesic attention bias for pairwise topology.
f1FL6lcnDV.key_idea: Combine equivariant local interactions and global attention with chirality conditioning and signed-volume supervision in a Cartesian flow model.
f1FL6lcnDV.evidence: Evaluation uses 1,000 held-out CREMP cyclic peptides containing four to six residues, including separate six-residue results.
f1FL6lcnDV.claimed_gains: CycPepFlow-L achieves 76.13% coverage F1; APG-L achieves 79.78% generated-set coverage precision and 0.419 Å matching distance, with 61.61% coverage F1 and 99.71% tetrahedral accuracy on six-residue peptides.

aXFGClr7QE.one_liner: Trajectory-level state-distribution correction, geometric-mean estimation, and length-aware clipping stabilize long-horizon language-model reinforcement learning.
aXFGClr7QE.problem: Token- or sequence-level policy-mismatch controls overlook trajectory-induced state-distribution shifts that can destabilize long-horizon language-model reinforcement learning.
aXFGClr7QE.method: TAPO derives a state-distribution correction from the off-policy policy gradient and incorporates it into the reinforcement-learning objective. A geometric-mean estimator reduces variance, while length-aware dynamic clipping limits overly deviated trajectory updates.
aXFGClr7QE.key_idea: Correct trajectory-induced state-distribution mismatch in the policy-gradient objective using geometric-mean estimation and length-aware clipping.
aXFGClr7QE.evidence: The paper derives the correction theoretically and evaluates mathematical reasoning and algorithmic coding across eight competition-level benchmarks.
aXFGClr7QE.claimed_gains: TAPO reports up to 48% and 12% improvement over GRPO on mathematical reasoning and algorithmic coding, respectively.

Ab5IBmIQod.one_liner: Separate query-key and value depth queries decouple attention routing in Block Attention Residuals.
Ab5IBmIQod.problem: Block Attention Residuals couples attention-score representations and aggregated value content by deriving queries, keys, and values from one shared depth mixture.
Ab5IBmIQod.method: RD-AttnRes retains the query-key depth route and learns a second depth query for values over the same block sources. Untying the queries adds one model-width vector per attention layer without extra projection or attention FLOPs.
Ab5IBmIQod.key_idea: Use independent depth queries for query-key representations and value representations over shared block sources.
Ab5IBmIQod.evidence: Experiments include five paired seeds at 120M and 343M parameters and matched three-seed 343M comparisons against additive and alternative depth-routing variants.
Ab5IBmIQod.claimed_gains: RD-AttnRes reports 2.97% and 2.43% lower perplexity than Block AttnRes at 120M and 343M, 4.7–9.6× larger NLL reductions than Six-block Delta (6.8× ratio of mean gains), and 4.44% lower perplexity than Six-block Delta-V.

7wCBpQ7Yhj.one_liner: A role-aware set encoder and unbalanced transport module predict product spectra directly from reactant and reagent spectra.
7wCBpQ7Yhj.problem: Variable unordered reaction inputs and non-conservative spectral changes complicate product-spectrum prediction without molecular-structure reconstruction.
7wCBpQ7Yhj.method: SpecReact encodes variable-sized spectral inputs with a role-aware set encoder. Its unbalanced optimal transport module models spectral correspondences and supplies structured supervision for reaction-induced peak and intensity changes.
7wCBpQ7Yhj.key_idea: Combine role-aware set encoding with unbalanced optimal transport to model reaction-induced correspondences when spectral peaks shift, appear, or disappear.
7wCBpQ7Yhj.evidence: A dataset pairs USPTO reactions with simulated IR spectra, and experiments on simulated and measured spectra compare reaction baselines and test spectral perturbations.

mi3dsGv6Ur.one_liner: Suppressing selected attention recipients while controlling redistributed mass isolates routing effects on representation cosine geometry.
mi3dsGv6Ur.problem: Attention-sink explanations conflict, and supposedly neutral non-sink controls can redirect removed attention mass onto sinks.
mi3dsGv6Ur.method: The study fixes inputs and model weights, suppresses selected attention recipients, and measures mean off-diagonal token cosine. It compares dose-matched controls with redistribution-blocked interventions and analyzes exact value-replacement updates and their first-order terms.
mi3dsGv6Ur.key_idea: Control where suppressed attention mass is redistributed before attributing changes in token cosine geometry to attention sinks.
mi3dsGv6Ur.evidence: Tests cover four language models and two corpora for control confounds, 16 language models for suppression direction, and Stable Diffusion 3 for text-recipient interventions.
mi3dsGv6Ur.claimed_gains: With redistribution blocked, sink effects are 2–8 times larger per removed mass where controls are measurable, while update-based predictions recover 73–74% of window-level signs.

3Kt188v0Yl.one_liner: Transferring a segmentation-pretrained decoder and aligning features to frozen DINOv2 guides RAW image demosaicing with scene structure.
3Kt188v0Yl.problem: Pixel-level demosaicing primarily uses low-level statistics and does not fully exploit structural information shared with visual understanding.
3Kt188v0Yl.method: SegDem pretrains region- and boundary-aware decoder representations through instance segmentation, then transfers the decoder to RAW-conditioned reconstruction. It anchors segmentation- and demosaicing-conditioned features in a shared frozen DINOv2 representation space.
3Kt188v0Yl.key_idea: Transfer an instance-segmentation decoder to RAW reconstruction while anchoring both tasks' features to frozen DINOv2 representations.
3Kt188v0Yl.evidence: Experiments cover convolutional, Transformer, and state-space backbones for Single- and Quad-Bayer demosaicing on synthetic, external, and challenging datasets.

V1r4op7aVG.one_liner: Predicting pretrained DINO representations and conditioning on those predictions guides flow matching without a second denoising trajectory.
V1r4op7aVG.problem: Co-denoising pretrained representations adds another ODE and requires representation-specific denoising schedules.
V1r4op7aVG.method: The flow model predicts a pretrained representation directly and conditions generation on its own prediction. This replaces representation co-denoising and removes the separate representation ODE and schedule.
V1r4op7aVG.key_idea: Directly predict pretrained representations and feed those predictions back as conditioning for the flow model.
V1r4op7aVG.evidence: ImageNet experiments compare training convergence and FID-based generation quality in latent and pixel spaces.
V1r4op7aVG.claimed_gains: On ImageNet, the method outperforms prior latent-space methods at 2× fewer epochs and improves over comparable pixel-space methods by more than 20%.

sF6pNak1tl.one_liner: Occasionally continuing beyond proposed stops trains later medical-image refinements and teaches a lightweight stopping head.
sF6pNak1tl.problem: Stopping training trajectories early removes supervision for later refinements, which can reinforce premature stopping.
sF6pNak1tl.method: StreamRefine models translation as an autoregressive stream of 3D refinement states conditioned on the source and prior predictions. Continue-to-Check training sometimes proceeds past proposed stops, supervising later refinements and a stopping head that weighs quality, anatomical drift, and computation.
sF6pNak1tl.key_idea: Continue selected training trajectories beyond proposed stops so skipped refinements and the stopping head learn the value of further computation.
sF6pNak1tl.evidence: Experiments across unspecified 3D medical translation tasks assess translation quality, anatomy-related performance, and efficiency, with analyses of continuation's effects on later refinements and stopping.

IjpLkj9Fn9.one_liner: Disagreement between fast and slow safety memories triggers monitor-state refreshes during streaming generation.
IjpLkj9Fn9.problem: Stale safety evidence delays unsafe-onset alarms and safe-state release after generation changes safety regimes.
IjpLkj9Fn9.method: HYSGUARD reads cross-layer hidden states and maintains fast and slow safety memories. Their discrepancy detects regime boundaries and refreshes only monitor state, while preserving the backbone and KV cache.
IjpLkj9Fn9.key_idea: Detect safety-regime boundaries from fast–slow memory discrepancy and selectively reset the monitor's stale evidence while preserving generation context.
IjpLkj9Fn9.evidence: The paper formalizes an O(r)-state online algorithm and evaluates controlled mechanisms and cross-model behavior using SWITCHTRACE's safe-to-unsafe, unsafe-to-safe, and repeated switches.

uPDG8ubICm.one_liner: REACH-breast enriches CT reports with MRI findings and aligns breast-region representations with side-specific textual evidence.
uPDG8ubICm.problem: Routine chest CT reports often omit low-contrast breast findings, and whole-volume contrastive learning can miss small, side-specific abnormalities.
uPDG8ubICm.method: REACH-breast enriches CT reports with CT-visible findings curated from temporally matched breast MRI reports. Hierarchical alignment connects left, right, bilateral, and global representations, while side-aware evidence-patch association links report evidence to breast regions within patches.
uPDG8ubICm.key_idea: Combine MRI-enriched CT reports with laterality-preserving hierarchical alignment and report-to-breast-patch associations.
uPDG8ubICm.evidence: BreastCT-12K contains 12,696 patients with routine chest CT scans, CT reports, and temporally matched breast MRI reports.

oBbcHhzxUD.one_liner: RecallNav stores original observations and learns goal-conditioned retrieval, recall decisions, and frontier selection from expert demonstrations.
oBbcHhzxUD.problem: Selective or compressed navigation memory can omit details needed by future goals, and retrieved evidence must guide revisiting versus exploration.
oBbcHhzxUD.method: RecallNav retains original observations and retrieves candidate frames using a frozen multimodal encoder. An MLLM reads retrieved, current, and frontier views in a bounded context and learns target grounding and search destinations with explicit evidence-linked recall supervision.
oBbcHhzxUD.key_idea: Separate unchanged observation storage from goal-conditioned retrieval and supervise recall decisions with the retrieved views that justify returning.
oBbcHhzxUD.evidence: GOAT-Bench and LMEE-Bench experiments compare navigation success and path efficiency, and stored RGB archives also support question answering through a separate pretrained MLLM.

U73JxjEsyY.one_liner: CondKD models teacher representations conditionally on student features, using split tokenization and label-guided distribution contraction.
U73JxjEsyY.problem: Deterministic distillation targets ignore transfer uncertainty, while conditional generation faces high-dimensional optimization and missing label supervision.
U73JxjEsyY.method: CondKD learns the conditional distribution of teacher representations given student representations.
