SplitTok supports unsupervised optimization, and Distribution Contraction incorporates labels into conditional reconstruction without explicit classification loss on multi-step sampled representations.
U73JxjEsyY.key_idea: Distill a conditional distribution of teacher features through split tokenization and label-driven contraction of the reconstruction distribution.
U73JxjEsyY.evidence: Theory analyzes Distribution Contraction as a stable multi-task gradient surrogate, and CC3M experiments compare unsupervised CondKD with a KL baseline.
U73JxjEsyY.claimed_gains: CondKD improves over the KL baseline by 16.29% under unsupervised KD on CC3M.

jE1lo0x7QI.one_liner: CORE removes site confounders, extracts shared connectivity scaffolds, and gates temporal line-graph message passing for brain-network generalization.
jE1lo0x7QI.problem: Site confounders obscure disease-related fMRI connectivity, while static connectivity omits informative within-scan variation.
jE1lo0x7QI.method: CORE residualizes site-specific confounders, extracts reproducible label-associated scaffold edges, and applies aggregated source deconfounders to unseen sites. Temporal edge descriptors feed a line graph whose message passing uses prior-guided subject-adaptive gating.
jE1lo0x7QI.key_idea: Combine site-residualized population connectivity scaffolds with temporal edge descriptors and subject-adaptive gated message passing.
jE1lo0x7QI.evidence: Leave-one-site-out experiments cover ABIDE, REST-meta-MDD, SRPBS, and ABCD, with repeated runs and a second ABIDE parcellation.
jE1lo0x7QI.claimed_gains: CORE reports up to a 9.4% relative improvement in accuracy averaged over repeated runs.

KKlgn78pde.one_liner: Parallel flow-matching processes jointly generate future observations and native controls for closed-loop gameplay and GUI interaction.
KKlgn78pde.problem: Game agents lack explicit dynamics models, while interactive game world models predict futures without functioning as task policies.
KKlgn78pde.method: GameWAM jointly generates visuals and keyboard-mouse actions using block-causal conditioning and flow matching, with per-step gameplay/GUI modes controlling action distributions and normalization. Block-cycle control predicts beyond the committed horizon, executes short blocks, and replans from new observations with hierarchical temporal context.
KKlgn78pde.key_idea: Jointly generate future visuals and mode-specific native actions, then execute short action blocks and replan within a block-cycle control loop.
KKlgn78pde.evidence: The paper constructs synchronized gameplay and GUI trajectories for joint world-action learning, but the supplied abstract does not report evaluation results.

dEwHXc3rTL.one_liner: Text-derived view anchors condition directional feature deformation for matching people between aerial and ground imagery.
dEwHXc3rTL.problem: Aerial-ground person matching must establish cross-view correspondence without losing identity-discriminative, view-specific cues.
dEwHXc3rTL.method: TAFD learns aerial and ground semantic anchors from shared and view-private prompts encoded by a frozen text encoder. Anchor differences condition separate directional operators that resample patch features, while target-space classifiers and stop-gradient identity prototypes supervise identity preservation.
dEwHXc3rTL.key_idea: Use differences between text-derived view anchors to predict directional spatial offsets for cross-view feature resampling under identity-consistency supervision.

5rbD6r70Pf.one_liner: Overspending-aware rewards train multi-turn agents to allocate resources across dynamically specified budgets.
5rbD6r70Pf.problem: External budget enforcement does not teach agents how to distribute limited resources across multi-turn tasks.
5rbD6r70Pf.method: BAPO compares eleven reward objectives, including adapted length penalties and new budget-aware formulations, in a shared training pipeline. Separate policies for each environment and resource type train across budget values to balance within-budget success and natural compliance.
5rbD6r70Pf.key_idea: Train across varying stated budgets with rewards that penalize overspending, allowing resource allocation to depend on budget and task difficulty.
5rbD6r70Pf.evidence: Qwen3.5 4B and 9B models train on AppWorld token, API-call, and step budgets and BabyAI turn budgets, with unseen-budget and zero-shot transfer evaluations.

tqmPXEtoDd.one_liner: A camera-LiDAR dataset varies scenes and extrinsics to benchmark cross-modal sensor calibration.
tqmPXEtoDd.problem: Homogeneous or closed-source calibration datasets limit validation and development of cross-modal sensor alignment methods.
tqmPXEtoDd.method: CalibBench constructs a diverse camera-LiDAR calibration dataset and evaluates prior methods on its challenging scenes and extrinsic settings. It also examines their performance after training.
tqmPXEtoDd.key_idea: Evaluate camera-LiDAR extrinsic estimation across varied scenes and sensor configurations within a shared calibration benchmark.
tqmPXEtoDd.evidence: The benchmark reports performance of previous calibration methods and their improvement after training, without numerical results in the abstract.

MXqyJatpLb.one_liner: Frequency-specific Kalman forecasts skip diffusion-transformer evaluations until predicted output uncertainty warrants recomputation.
MXqyJatpLb.problem: Uniform feature forecasts ignore frequency-dependent evolution and nonuniform denoising progress, accumulating errors when many steps are skipped.
MXqyJatpLb.method: SpecKCast applies a 2D DCT to model outputs and tracks each coefficient's value and rate with a lightweight Kalman filter. Band-specific time coordinates derive from the noise schedule, and forecast uncertainty determines when to evaluate the transformer.
MXqyJatpLb.key_idea: Track DCT coefficients with Kalman filters on band-specific noise-schedule time coordinates and trigger transformer evaluations from forecast uncertainty.
MXqyJatpLb.evidence: Experiments compare acceleration-fidelity trade-offs against caching and forecasting methods on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-14B, and HunyuanVideo.

6kMvoKMrX3.one_liner: Cortical-level perturbations and hierarchy-conditioned reconstruction adapt fMRI decoding from visual perception to mental imagery.
6kMvoKMrX3.problem: Perception-trained fMRI decoders degrade on imagery because information shifts across cortical levels and stimulus-specific structural-semantic preferences.
6kMvoKMrX3.method: Wallbreaker perturbs and redistributes cortical-level representations during training to simulate hierarchy shifts. During reconstruction, it infers each stimulus's hierarchy preference and adjusts the balance between semantic guidance and structural anchoring.
6kMvoKMrX3.key_idea: Simulate cortical hierarchy shifts during training and infer stimulus-specific hierarchy preferences to balance semantic and structural reconstruction signals.
6kMvoKMrX3.evidence: The abstract reports improved imagery reconstruction metrics alongside competitive vision reconstruction, without named datasets or numerical results.

RNkUvnXetH.one_liner: A training regularizer aligns unconditional MoE activations with the conditional subspace to limit classifier-free guidance collapse.
RNkUvnXetH.problem: Independent expert routing places conditional and unconditional activations in different subspaces, amplifying off-subspace residuals at high guidance scales.
RNkUvnXetH.method: SAGE regularizes unconditional MoE activations toward the conditional expert subspace during training without restricting routing diversity. This alignment adds no inference cost.
RNkUvnXetH.key_idea: Project unconditional MoE activations toward the conditional expert subspace during training to constrain residuals amplified by classifier-free guidance.
RNkUvnXetH.evidence: Toy experiments measure extreme drift, and a 1B-parameter text-to-image model evaluates generation quality with DPG-Bench.
RNkUvnXetH.claimed_gains: SAGE suppresses extreme drift by 9.2× in toy experiments and boosts peak DPG-Bench performance by 9.3% in a 1B-parameter text-to-image model.

6PlfDcC0PM.one_liner: Differentiable sparse-support selection jointly quantizes MoE weights, while grouped sparse kernels execute the compressed experts on Sparse Tensor Cores.
6PlfDcC0PM.problem: MoE compression with hardware-supported sparsity and low precision suffers quality loss and lacks grouped sparse matrix-multiplication primitives.
6PlfDcC0PM.method: MoESQ continuously reparameterizes discrete semi-structured support and jointly optimizes it with quantized weights under router-weighted reconstruction, using expert-parallel compression. A custom grouped sparse GEMM kernel executes the resulting low-precision sparse experts on Sparse Tensor Cores.
6PlfDcC0PM.key_idea: Jointly optimize relaxed semi-structured sparsity and quantized weights under router-weighted reconstruction, then execute them with a grouped sparse GEMM kernel.
6PlfDcC0PM.evidence: Evaluations span MoEs from 30 billion to trillion-scale parameters, with system benchmarks on NVIDIA B200 GPUs.
6PlfDcC0PM.claimed_gains: MoESQ improves joint sparse-quantization task accuracy by up to 4.35 percentage points while preserving 96.09% of the original models' performance.

obt59DdVCm.one_liner: Value-only speculative drafting delegates fixed schema tokens to a state machine and treats them as certain during verification.
obt59DdVCm.problem: Structured-generation speculative decoding wastes draft positions on predetermined syntax and risks unnecessary rejection of fixed schema tokens.
obt59DdVCm.method: DChord's PairDraft predicts field values and end markers while a pair state machine expands them into full serialized drafts. PairCut uses schema certainty in concurrent-serving verification decisions to extend acceptance with little additional target latency.
obt59DdVCm.key_idea: Predict only field values and end markers, insert deterministic structure through a state machine, and account for that certainty during verification.
obt59DdVCm.evidence: Evaluation covers Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and Gemma4-12B across four schema-determined tasks with multimodal and text-only inputs, including autoregressive comparisons.

PJ3ZdImcJM.one_liner: Paired harmful and benign requests train explicit risk judgments before actions, with equal penalties for over-refusal and unsafe compliance.
PJ3ZdImcJM.problem: Harmful-request-only safety benchmarks conceal excessive refusal of benign requests that resemble harmful ones.
PJ3ZdImcJM.method: Reason-Judge-Act uses multi-turn RL on harmful-benign pairs sharing surface forms but differing in intent. Each turn requires reasoning, a dedicated risk judgment, and action; balanced penalties and corrective feedback support later revisions.
PJ3ZdImcJM.key_idea: Train explicit risk decisions on surface-matched harmful-benign pairs, equally penalizing unsafe compliance and over-refusal across feedback-driven turns.
PJ3ZdImcJM.evidence: Experiments on six backbones from two model families compare discernment and reasoning preservation, with an additional analysis of released DeepSeek-R1-Distill checkpoints.

hbYaXsickP.one_liner: Majorization-minimization surrogate saddle points reduce min-max optimization to single-variable problems before neural unrolling.
hbYaXsickP.problem: Neural approaches to saddle-point problems face unstable two-player optimization or lose tightness through relaxed proxy objectives.
hbYaXsickP.method: RUN replaces each iteration's min-max problem with a surrogate convex in the primal variable and concave in the dual. Closed-form dual elimination yields minimization, while primal elimination and a Sion-licensed operator exchange yield maximization.
hbYaXsickP.key_idea: Construct convex-concave surrogate saddle points and eliminate one variable to obtain single-variable objectives suitable for neural unrolling.
hbYaXsickP.evidence: The supplied abstract describes two analytical reductions of surrogate saddle points, including an operator exchange justified by Sion's minimax theorem.

VNxlRjx7yG.one_liner: Local convolutional memory aggregation replaces global attention for promptable image and video segmentation.
VNxlRjx7yG.problem: High-resolution encoding and global memory attention make SAM 2 costly, motivating faster memory operations when cross-frame correspondence is local.
VNxlRjx7yG.method: FastSAM2 uses a fully convolutional architecture whose Cross-frame Convolutional Aggregation combines temporal mixing, same-position similarity gates, depthwise propagation, memory weighting, and gated fusion. It trains only on public SA-1B and SA-V annotations without pseudo-labels or distillation.
VNxlRjx7yG.key_idea: Aggregate cross-frame memory through local convolutional propagation and content-conditioned gating without constructing a global query-key matrix.
VNxlRjx7yG.evidence: Evaluations include LVIS with ground-truth boxes and categories, steady-state video propagation across three GPUs, operator comparisons, and shared-evaluator LVOS v2 tests including reappearance after at least one second of absence.
VNxlRjx7yG.claimed_gains: FastSAM2 reaches 51.7 mask AP on LVIS and 132.5 frames/s at 1024×1024 on H20 versus 41.6 for SAM 2 B+, with 3.18-3.20x speedup across three GPUs; LVOS v2 full-set/reappearance scores are 76.9/59.7 versus SAM2Long's 85.0/69.0.

SobP24aBq7.one_liner: Variance-reduced reward guidance, clean-token logit tilting, and adaptive particle selection steer frozen discrete diffusion models.
SobP24aBq7.problem: Combined guidance-and-search samplers use noisy estimates and fixed selection settings without accounting for their target distribution.
SobP24aBq7.method: VGAS identifies the combined sampler's target distribution and reduces guidance-estimate variance. It applies reward tilting to clean-token logits to preserve the pretrained schedule and adjusts selection temperature at each step.
SobP24aBq7.key_idea: Coordinate variance-reduced guidance with clean-token reward tilting and per-step selection temperatures under the combined sampler's target distribution.
SobP24aBq7.evidence: Regulatory DNA, protein, and small-molecule benchmarks compare training-free reward against other samplers and a reward-fine-tuned generator.

PJnDxPEjb8.one_liner: Shared depth-grounded latent states connect RGB-D spatial completion with action-conditioned future-feature prediction.
PJnDxPEjb8.problem: Robot manipulation representations must connect scene geometry with changes caused by actions.
PJnDxPEjb8.method: DepState-JEPA builds on V-JEPA 2.1, aggregating shared RGB-depth features into a metric 3D state while retaining private features only for visual decoding. Calibrated ray queries and action-conditioned transitions support decoding, while robot-state readouts, object trajectories, and forward-kinematics supervision shape state learning.
PJnDxPEjb8.key_idea: Separate shared depth-grounded state from modality-private decoding memory, then transition the shared state under actions to predict future RGB and depth features.
PJnDxPEjb8.evidence: The supplied abstract names evaluations of RGB-encoder transfer, RGB-D feature completion, and visual forecasting, but provides no complete results.

oV5FpLBWJn.one_liner: Second-order message residuals and learned corrections recurrently update node-local geometry for graph propagation.
oV5FpLBWJn.problem: Geometry estimated from aggregated graph features can miss individual-message variation and dependencies between feature dimensions.
oV5FpLBWJn.method: GeoF maintains a positive-definite geometry per node in block log-triangular coordinates and uses it for neighborhood weighting and frame transport. Second-order aligned-message residuals and a shared learned controller drive bounded geometry updates that affect subsequent propagation on a fixed topology.
oV5FpLBWJn.key_idea: Feed second-order residual statistics of transported messages into bounded positive-definite geometry updates that determine the next propagation step.

z4H49rxpb2.one_liner: Stage-specific reconstruction representations benchmark when poisoning signals become detectable in 3D Gaussian Splatting.
z4H49rxpb2.problem: 3DGS studies emphasize attack success while overlooking detection signals that emerge or change across reconstruction stages.
z4H49rxpb2.method: Poison-3DGS organizes base scenes and poisoned variants for stage-wise detection analysis. It exposes intermediate representations from the reconstruction pipeline, including multi-view images, SfM geometry, and training dynamics.
z4H49rxpb2.key_idea: Evaluate poisoning detectability across the heterogeneous intermediate representations produced at successive stages of 3DGS reconstruction.
z4H49rxpb2.evidence: The benchmark contains 100 base scenes and 1,253 poisoned variants for stage-wise detection characterization.

ulYwPJpjWD.one_liner: Serialization-aware storage metrics and fixed-trace controls measure retained agent data and persistence-layer amplification.
ulYwPJpjWD.problem: Agent benchmarks omit post-run storage, and raw byte measurements conceal duplication introduced or obscured by persistence formats.
ulYwPJpjWD.method: AgentFootprint measures retention, channel composition, duplication, growth, compressibility, and conversation-history reconstructability across frameworks. Replaying identical scripted content through persistence adapters separates storage amplification from differences in agent behavior.
ulYwPJpjWD.key_idea: Decode serialization effects when measuring retained data and replay fixed traces across adapters to isolate persistence-layer amplification.
ulYwPJpjWD.evidence: The benchmark covers eight agent frameworks, with fixed-trace controls and matched-model, matched-tool, matched-task comparisons of LangGraph and OpenAI Agents.
ulYwPJpjWD.claimed_gains: Fixed-trace retained sizes differ by 6.7×, while LangGraph and OpenAI Agents both achieve 100% accuracy yet differ by 15.7× in default retention.

FhgHApRWBT.one_liner: Influence-ranked anchor tokens receive fresh KV states while diffusion language models reuse shared affix caches across requests.
FhgHApRWBT.problem: Bidirectional attention makes shared-context KV states depend on tokens under generation, so direct cache reuse becomes stale.
FhgHApRWBT.method: ACache selects request-specific Anchor Tokens by their influence on masked generation regions and recomputes only those affix KV states. Its inference engine reads these states alongside a common affix cache shared across concurrent requests, including prefixes, infixes, and suffixes.
FhgHApRWBT.key_idea: Recompute KV states only for influential request-specific affix tokens while sharing the remaining affix cache across requests.
FhgHApRWBT.evidence: Comparisons assess accuracy against direct reuse and prior selection criteria, and latency and throughput against the same engine with intra-request caching only.
FhgHApRWBT.claimed_gains: Recomputing around 20% of affix tokens recovers most lost accuracy on average; ACache cuts recompute latency by up to 56.7% and reaches as much as 1.71× end-to-end throughput.

tD8P7Oc8wn.one_liner: Iterative multi-agent generation combines persistent trajectory memory with reusable domain skills.
tD8P7Oc8wn.problem: Multimodal generators struggle to follow complex instructions and perform specialized downstream tasks.
tD8P7Oc8wn.method: GEMS runs a structured multi-agent optimization loop with persistent memory of factual states and compressed experiential summaries. A shared skill repository supplies reusable domain guidance within the same generation workflow.
tD8P7Oc8wn.key_idea: Iteratively refine multimodal generations using hierarchical trajectory memory and reusable domain guidance from a shared skill repository.
tD8P7Oc8wn.evidence: Experiments cover five mainstream and four downstream tasks across multiple generative backends, including Z-Image-Turbo and Nano Banana 2 comparisons on GenEval2.
tD8P7Oc8wn.claimed_gains: GEMS enables the 6B Z-Image-Turbo model to match Nano Banana 2 on GenEval2.

AST8kyBlc8.one_liner: Self-distillation specializes any-order image generation using per-image token orders extracted from the model's confidence.
AST8kyBlc8.problem: Any-order autoregressive image models spread finite capacity across permutations, sacrificing sample quality despite their editing flexibility.
AST8kyBlc8.method: OAR extracts a content-dependent generation order for each training image from a pretrained any-order model's confidence scores. Fine-tuning on image-order pairs concentrates training on those trajectories while preserving any-order conditionals.
AST8kyBlc8.key_idea: Extract one high-confidence generation trajectory per image and fine-tune the any-order model on the resulting image-order pairs.
AST8kyBlc8.evidence: Class-conditional ImageNet 256×256 experiments compare the any-order baseline and random-to-raster annealing under matched evaluation, alongside zero-shot inpainting and outpainting.
AST8kyBlc8.claimed_gains: OAR improves ImageNet 256×256 FID from 2.39 to 2.17, compared with 2.34 for random-to-raster annealing on the same backbone.

lJ4TRPpUvr.one_liner: Alternating agent-program revisions and model reinforcement learning couple scientific-agent execution improvements with training.
lJ4TRPpUvr.problem: Scientific-agent improvement requires understanding how program adaptation and model learning interact and depend on update order.
lJ4TRPpUvr.method: ScienceBuddy's inner loop revises the agent program with the model fixed using interaction feedback, while its outer loop trains the model on fresh verifier-scored rollouts under the revised program. Repeating these cycles lets program changes shape training and model changes support further program adaptation.
lJ4TRPpUvr.key_idea: Alternate feedback-guided full-program revisions at fixed model weights with reinforcement learning from verifier-scored rollouts under the revised program.
lJ4TRPpUvr.evidence: Experiments cover seven scientific task categories, crossed training/evaluation programs, equal-count update-order controls, and reply-availability and editing-scope controls.
lJ4TRPpUvr.claimed_gains: The two-cycle ScienceBuddy system reaches 70.4% Test accuracy from a 43.2% initial baseline.

ZgMCyyu2SR.one_liner: Action-sensitive latent predictions and a learned deliberation gate select robot actions using task progress and rollout consistency.
ZgMCyyu2SR.problem: World action models can waste computation on nuisance variation or select inaccurate imagined futures using progress-only scores.
ZgMCyyu2SR.method: ADEPT learns a token mask for action-dependent information and trains autoregressive latent predictions across multiple steps. A heuristic-distilled gate triggers candidate evaluation using predicted progress and rollout consistency.
ZgMCyyu2SR.key_idea: Mask action-dependent latent information and gate candidate rollouts scored jointly by predicted task progress and consistency.
ZgMCyyu2SR.evidence: Experiments evaluate LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, and six real-robot tasks, including matched frozen-prior and direct-scoring controls.
ZgMCyyu2SR.claimed_gains: ADEPT reaches 99.1% LIBERO success, 88.1% LIBERO-Plus Macro-7 (16.6 percentage points above its frozen prior and 3.1 percentage points above an 85.0% direct scorer), 25.5% RoboCasa365 split-macro success, and 90.3% versus 55.3% real-robot success, while reducing planning latency by 25–32% at 3.1–3.5× reactive latency.

akoBBb2W7I.one_liner: Online self-supervised fast-weight updates compress observation history into action-trained memory for robotic manipulation.
akoBBb2W7I.problem: Memory-dependent robot tasks require retaining action-relevant information that disappears from current observations.
akoBBb2W7I.method: T²MEM updates compact fast weights online using self-supervised test-time training and supplies retrieved context to a pretrained vision-language-action policy through an observation-grounded interface. Action supervision and alternating memory-policy optimization shape retention and use.
akoBBb2W7I.key_idea: Encode observation history in fast weights through online self-supervision while action supervision trains memory retention and retrieval.
akoBBb2W7I.evidence: Evaluation covers 16 RoboMME tasks, comparisons with recurrent-memory methods, and controlled inference profiling against explicit methods.
akoBBb2W7I.claimed_gains: Average success increases from 17.93% to 56.83% over the memory-free base policy, with at least 3x inference speedup over explicit methods.

prICES3UDY.one_liner: Majorization-minimization jointly assigns image lines and estimates Manhattan-world rotations without relaxing the original optimization problem.
prICES3UDY.problem: Single-image Manhattan rotation estimation must jointly resolve noisy line assignments and orthogonal scene directions.
prICES3UDY.method: MMVP directly minimizes truncated multi-selection error over the rotation group. Its surrogate freezes associations, uses homotopy-guided outlier handling for truncation, and replaces the quadratic form with a linear function admitting a closed-form minimizer.
prICES3UDY.key_idea: Alternate fixed line associations with homotopy-guided truncation majorization and a closed-form linear surrogate minimization over rotations.
prICES3UDY.evidence: The supplied abstract derives a surrogate with per-update cost linear in the number of lines; its theorem statement is truncated and experimental settings are not stated.

3zoF8U8kJ8.one_liner: Hidden optimization instances and exact checkers test whether tool-using agents turn acquired information into globally optimal decisions.
3zoF8U8kJ8.problem: Tool-use benchmarks reward feasible workflows without testing whether decisions optimize shared constraints and costs globally.
3zoF8U8kJ8.method: AlgoWorlds exposes hidden combinatorial instances through sequential information-tool calls before agents commit to one structured decision. Deterministic generators and exact algorithms certify instances, while an independent checker measures feasibility, objective value, and optimality.
3zoF8U8kJ8.key_idea: Hide certified optimization instances behind information tools and check the agent's final decision against the exact global optimum.
3zoF8U8kJ8.evidence: AlgoWorlds contains 240 environments spanning ten combinatorial optimization families and four workload levels, with two structurally different tool interfaces per instance.

KVNlfq7GAO.one_liner: A GRU predicts robot-policy failure from evolving action entropy, temporal coherence, and action–state coupling.
KVNlfq7GAO.problem: Robot failure detectors need to generalize across policies and environments while explaining why rollouts fail.
KVNlfq7GAO.method: The paper models VLA control as an information pipeline, derives eight metrics, and selects the Tri-Info combination of action entropy, temporal action coherence, and action–state coupling. A GRU tracks these signals to predict failures.
KVNlfq7GAO.key_idea: Predict failure from temporal changes in action entropy, action-history coherence, and action–state information coupling.
KVNlfq7GAO.evidence: Experiments cover multiple VLA models, simulated benchmarks, real-world tasks, and transfer across architectures, environments, and simulation-to-reality without target-domain failure labels.
KVNlfq7GAO.claimed_gains: Tri-Info reaches over 70% accuracy on real-world tasks.

EwsJVDO5Vg.one_liner: Worst-case variance retention selects sparse features while protecting the weakest target principal component.
EwsJVDO5Vg.problem: Trace-based sparse principal subspace estimation can spend its feature budget on strong components and leave another direction with no variance.
EwsJVDO5Vg.method: The paper optimizes the smallest retained-variance fraction across target population directions under feature restriction. It characterizes support attainment and the target eigenspace, and distinguishes this criterion from taking a minimum over estimated basis columns.
EwsJVDO5Vg.key_idea: Select a sparse support by maximizing the minimum fraction of variance retained across the target population directions.
EwsJVDO5Vg.evidence: Theoretical covariance examples expose degenerate trace maximizers, while support and eigenspace results characterize the proposed criterion and Schur–Horn analysis explains the basis-column alternative.

AUOn1tuzCX.one_liner: Tracking persistent spectral modes lets SPLIT redistribute attention-head gains while conserving reference energy.
AUOn1tuzCX.problem: Multimodal reasoning can drift from visual evidence while existing remedies depend on fixed heads or inaccessible fused-attention intermediates.
AUOn1tuzCX.method: SPLIT tracks a dominant residual-space mode whose spectral share persists as its carrier heads change. Its training-free controller redistributes gain toward the head bulk with exact reference-energy conservation.
AUOn1tuzCX.key_idea: Track persistent spectral concentration across changing carrier heads and redistribute head gains while conserving reference energy.
AUOn1tuzCX.evidence: Analyses compare spectral patterns across three models, prove properties of the controller, and evaluate five models on eight benchmarks against five recent baselines.

5WbHJ1SWCZ.one_liner: Hadamard-mixed weight quantization combines with divergence-tail calibration sampling to preserve low-bit language-model predictions.
5WbHJ1SWCZ.problem: Extreme scalar weight quantization must preserve predictive behavior despite few reconstruction levels and limited calibration samples.
5WbHJ1SWCZ.method: FidelityQ mixes weight rows with randomized Hadamard transforms and fits mirrored four-level minimum-distortion quantizers that decompose into two sign-valued bases. Knowledge-Intensive Calibration ranks sequences by the tail of teacher-student token divergence and selects the highest-scoring samples.
5WbHJ1SWCZ.key_idea: Fit symmetric quantizers after Hadamard mixing and prioritize calibration sequences with large teacher-student divergence tails.
5WbHJ1SWCZ.evidence: The paper gives an exact two-sign-basis decomposition and analyzes heavy-tailed predictive discrepancies concentrated on confidently predicted teacher tokens; numerical evaluation results are not stated.

XTajRLp0Fz.one_liner: Resumption and rollback experiments test whether agent memories reconstruct interrupted task state without repeating or skipping work.
XTajRLp0Fz.problem: Existing memory benchmarks assess reuse across tasks rather than recovery of interrupted tasks with preserved or rolled-back progress.
XTajRLp0Fz.method: RecoverMemBench measures recovery rates and extra costs relative to uninterrupted runs. Task resumption tests state reconstruction with preserved progress, while rollback tests recognition of lost progress and retention of reusable information.
XTajRLp0Fz.key_idea: Compare memory-based recovery with uninterrupted runs under both preserved-progress resumption and environment rollback.
XTajRLp0Fz.evidence: Evaluation of 11 memory systems identifies failures in retrieving recovery-relevant records and distinguishing rolled-back work from completed work.
XTajRLp0Fz.claimed_gains: Existing systems average below 50% recovery in both settings and over 150% additional rollback steps, while the proposed memory system improves recovery rates by over 35%.

PFfM7tEwTn.one_liner: Stage-specific utility predictors separately admit pooled evidence to search agents and final-answer writers.
PFfM7tEwTn.problem: Evidence useful for continued search can differ from evidence useful for writing the final answer.
PFfM7tEwTn.method: StageAdmit retains every collected item in an evidence pool and trains stage-specific predictor heads on paired keep-mask comparisons. Separate policies choose evidence for search panels and the writer's panel using effects on answer quality, tool calls, and final-answer marginal gains.
PFfM7tEwTn.key_idea: Retain all evidence but learn separate admission masks from keep-versus-mask utility comparisons for search and answer generation.
PFfM7tEwTn.evidence: Experiments on WideSearch and GISA compare StageAdmit with evaluated baselines using GLM-5.
PFfM7tEwTn.claimed_gains: StageAdmit surpasses the strongest baseline by 1.5 and 1.6 Item-F1 points on WideSearch and GISA with GLM-5 while reducing completion time by 13.1%.

GhghP7h0cq.one_liner: A persistent graph of evidence, hypotheses, interventions, and outcomes governs iterative agent-runtime optimization.
GhghP7h0cq.problem: Proposer-centered runtime optimization forces an LLM to reconstruct evolving experimental logic from an expanding history.
GhghP7h0cq.method: Causal Improvement Graph stores improvement state in linked EVIDENCE, HYPOTHESIS, INTERVENTION, and OUTCOME nodes. Local proposers use these relations to determine subsequent runtime revisions and evaluations.
GhghP7h0cq.key_idea: Represent optimization history as linked evidence, hypothesis, intervention, and outcome nodes that directly guide local revision proposals.
GhghP7h0cq.evidence: The supplied abstract mentions evaluation across agent tasks but does not specify tasks, settings, or results.

kahtIGYnAX.one_liner: Cross-video action and frame prediction learns transferable interactions from task-paired human demonstrations.
kahtIGYnAX.problem: Within-video next-frame prediction can exploit shared appearance instead of learning interactions that transfer across scenes and embodiments.
kahtIGYnAX.method: WATCH conditions on one demonstration's video and actions to predict another demonstration's actions and future frames from its current observation. Pretraining uses task-paired egocentric human videos without matched human–robot demonstrations, followed by robot post-training.
kahtIGYnAX.key_idea: Predict one demonstration's future actions and frames using another task-matched demonstration across changes in scene and demonstrator.
kahtIGYnAX.evidence: Analyses test cross-embodiment motion alignment and unseen-robot prediction before post-training, followed by MimicDroid and context-free tests across robot embodiments.
kahtIGYnAX.claimed_gains: WATCH improves MimicDroid in-context success from 40.9% to 68.3% with Cosmos Policy and from 59.8% to 77.7% with Cosmos3.

tTVCic69Jm.one_liner: Joint image–geometry attention repeatedly exchanges information between per-view image features and shared 3D geometry during denoising.
tTVCic69Jm.problem: Image-conditioned 3D generation must preserve visible image details while integrating complementary views consistently.
tTVCic69Jm.method: ImaGeo combines per-view image and geometry self-attention with joint attention that connects all views to shared geometry. Updated image features carry geometry and cross-view context into later blocks, trained through geometry flow matching without input camera parameters.
tTVCic69Jm.key_idea: Alternate per-view processing with joint image–geometry attention so updated image features carry shared geometric context into subsequent denoising blocks.
tTVCic69Jm.evidence: Experiments use GSO, Toys4K, AI-generated images, and controlled single-view fine-stage comparisons with parameter-matched and larger baselines.
tTVCic69Jm.claimed_gains: A 1.5B denoiser outperforms a parameter-matched cross-attention baseline and achieves normal-map quality comparable to a 5B baseline.

mWMreS5aiw.one_liner: Attaches a parallel recurrent memory branch to a full-attention LLM to maintain persistent internal state across context turnovers.
mWMreS5aiw.problem: External text-retrieval memory systems leave LLM inference stateless across context turnovers and restrict preserved information to verbalized text records.
mWMreS5aiw.method: LiveMem augments a pretrained full-attention LLM with a parallel recurrent memory branch that updates an internal memory state online and persists it across context turnovers while full attention serves a bounded working window. Memory-oriented post-training teaches the model to read from and maintain this persistent state after source evidence leaves the context.
mWMreS5aiw.key_idea: Pairs exact full attention over a bounded working window with an online-updated parallel recurrent branch whose persistent state survives context eviction.
mWMreS5aiw.evidence: Evaluated against RAG and intrinsic memory baselines on LongMemEval—including settings where supporting evidence is removed from active context—and test-time learning tasks.

3QvbUC8rfA.one_liner: Disentangles causal and style representations to reweight frozen source-domain classifiers at inference using unlabeled target style distributions.
3QvbUC8rfA.problem: Domain generalization methods enforcing invariant prediction fail when the conditional relationship between causal representations and labels varies across domains.
3QvbUC8rfA.method: LADDER learns disentangled causal and style encoders, freezes them, and fits source-specific classifiers on each training domain. At inference, it uses an unlabeled set of target-domain covariates to match style distributions and compute combination weights over the fixed source classifiers without target labels or parameter updates.
3QvbUC8rfA.key_idea: Uses the style distribution of unlabeled target-domain covariates at test time to compute mixture weights over fixed source-specific causal classifiers without parameter updates.
3QvbUC8rfA.evidence: Supported by theoretical source-reweighting guarantees and experiments on synthetic simulations, FMoW, and a location-grouped iWildCam benchmark.

Xer1DvcbXV.one_liner: Evaluates coding agents' selective help-seeking judgment on tasks with exploration-revealed specification blockers using Ask-F1 precision-recall scoring.
Xer1DvcbXV.problem: Existing coding agent benchmarks provide complete unambiguous specifications and score only execution correctness, failing to distinguish lucky guesses from appropriate clarification requests.
Xer1DvcbXV.method: HiL-Bench introduces software engineering and text-to-SQL tasks containing human-validated missing, ambiguous, and contradictory blockers that surface only through progressive exploration, scoring selective escalation via Ask-F1 (harmonic mean of question precision and blocker recall). Reinforcement learning is also applied to reduce this help-seeking judgment gap.
Xer1DvcbXV.key_idea: Embeds missing, ambiguous, and contradictory blockers that surface only during exploration into coding tasks and scores selective human escalation via Ask-F1.
Xer1DvcbXV.evidence: Evaluates frontier coding agents across software engineering (SWE) and text-to-SQL domains alongside failure-pattern analysis and reinforcement learning experiments.

pmFcvQ3ItS.one_liner: Derives dynamical mean-field equations with router Onsager corrections and Random-Energy-Model mappings for high-dimensional Mixture-of-Experts training dynamics.
pmFcvQ3ItS.problem: The coupled high-dimensional feature-learning dynamics of routing mechanisms and expert weights—and how temperature and initialization govern specialization—remain analytically uncharacterized in Mixture-of-Experts layers.
pmFcvQ3ItS.method: The authors apply dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) to an E-expert MoE layer, closing non-Gaussian routing actions with a Gaussian routing-field approximation and incorporating a router-specific Onsager correction. They map softmax gating to a Random Energy Model in a signal-dependent field to separate saddle-point initialization amplification from thermodynamic router condensation.
pmFcvQ3ItS.key_idea: Closes high-dimensional MoE feature-learning DMFT equations with a Gaussian routing-field approximation and router Onsager term while mapping softmax gating to a signal-dependent Random Energy Model.
pmFcvQ3ItS.evidence: Validated theoretically and numerically against gradient-flow simulations with E = 2, 4, and 8 experts across cold and warm routing temperatures.

i0Un1bB1kX.one_liner: Prunes 3D Gaussian Splatting primitives by estimating rendering distortion along opacity-dissolution and geometric-collapse paths via randomized Gauss-Newton projections.
i0Un1bB1kX.problem: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting post-pruning methods rely on heuristic attributes, rendering weights, or generic parameter sensitivity rather than measuring the rendering distortion caused by removing a Gaussian.
i0Un1bB1kX.method: VanishGS models primitive disappearance along two complementary perturbation paths—opacity dissolution and geometric collapse—to capture both appearance and geometric impact. It estimates directional rendering distortion along these paths using the Gauss-Newton matrix with diagonal entries approximated via randomized projections.
i0Un1bB1kX.key_idea: Measures per-Gaussian removal distortion along coupled opacity-dissolution and geometric-collapse perturbations using randomized-projection approximations of the Gauss-Newton diagonal.
i0Un1bB1kX.evidence: Evaluated across multiple 3D Gaussian Splatting benchmarks, pruning ratios, and post-compression pipelines.

NLXgdOlPSb.one_liner: Separates block-drafting information floors from model gaps and introduces a predecessor-conditioned prefix-attention head for speculative decoding.
NLXgdOlPSb.problem: Accepted-length metrics in parallel block speculative decoding conflate irreducible rejection from missing within-block token dependencies with drafter modeling errors on observable context.
NLXgdOlPSb.method: The authors define a conditioning-order information floor to separate intrinsic parallel-blindness rejection from model gaps, showing that conditioning on a single realized predecessor removes 86–100% of the parallel floor. Guided by this locality, they replace context-independent predecessor correction with a prefix-attention head that reads committed context conditional on the predecessor.
NLXgdOlPSb.key_idea: Defines conditioning-order information floors to isolate parallel-blindness rejection from model gaps and replaces context-independent predecessor corrections with a predecessor-conditioned prefix-attention head.
NLXgdOlPSb.evidence: Measured across four domains, four open-weight targets (including Qwen3-4B against DFlash and DSpark), and a frontier API target, plus serving evaluation on Qwen3-4B across nine tasks.
NLXgdOlPSb.claimed_gains: Improves mean serving accepted length on Qwen3-4B by 3.93% over the released DSpark checkpoint across nine tasks, after finding one realized token removes 86–100% of the 0.286 final-slot parallel floor.

H06DYKLn0K.one_liner: Transfers multi-level search representations from a past-current-future ground-truth crop teacher to a past-template visual tracker with reliability weighting.
H06DYKLn0K.problem: Visual object trackers at deployment must trade off exact initial ground-truth templates that grow stale against fresh recent templates cropped from uncertain predictions.
H06DYKLn0K.method: Privileged Appearance Transfer for Tracking (PATT) trains a student tracker receiving only past-frame templates to predict multi-level search representations of a privileged teacher that observes exact ground-truth target crops from past, current, and future frames. Transfer weights scale with the teacher's localization accuracy and advantage over the student, and all teacher modules are discarded at deployment.
H06DYKLn0K.key_idea: Trains a past-template student tracker to predict multi-level representations of a privileged teacher observing exact past, current, and future target crops, weighted by teacher localization reliability.
H06DYKLn0K.evidence: Motivated by a current-frame ground-truth target-crop oracle experiment on LaSOT demonstrating a 15.2 percentage point AUC gap.

l7Ttu4cLwb.one_liner: Combines hybrid continuous-spike temporal memory with recurrent binary-state refinement and confidence-based early exit for spiking speech command recognition.
l7Ttu4cLwb.problem: Fixed computation paths in spiking neural networks for speech command recognition spend redundant compute on easy inputs and obscure how predictions evolve over inference steps.
l7Ttu4cLwb.method: SpikCTU builds a fixed temporal memory via a hybrid continuous-and-spike embedding and repeatedly queries it with a shared Continuous Thinking Unit that updates a binary recurrent state through lightweight stage adapters. Stepwise accumulated prediction corrections support either full-step learned aggregation or confidence-based early exit.
l7Ttu4cLwb.key_idea: Repeatedly query a hybrid spike-and-continuous temporal memory with a shared thinking unit to accumulate prediction corrections and trigger confidence-based early exit.
l7Ttu4cLwb.evidence: Evaluated on three speech command recognition benchmarks alongside trajectory and attention analyses of multi-step error correction.
l7Ttu4cLwb.claimed_gains: SpikCTU achieves competitive accuracy using 0.16-0.17M parameters while confidence-based early exit further reduces computational cost without sacrificing accuracy.

NfCZJAaQdb.one_liner: Audits video anomaly benchmarks by translating field contracts into video, text, cross-text, and alignment checks to compute joint usability.
NfCZJAaQdb.problem: Language annotations in video anomaly understanding benchmarks suffer from unmeasured video-text alignment and granularity failures when evaluated without respect to native field specifications.
NfCZJAaQdb.method: The contract-aware audit framework translates native annotation field requirements into scoped diagnostic questions covering video quality, standalone text quality, cross-text consistency, and video-text alignment, linking them to compute conditional joint usability.
NfCZJAaQdb.key_idea: Translate field-specific annotation contracts into scoped diagnostic questions across video, text, consistency, and alignment to measure conditional joint usability and guide rewrites.
NfCZJAaQdb.evidence: Audits 7,928 videos and 56,103 video-text pairs across nine benchmarks and tests downstream VALU multiple-choice accuracy after fine-tuning on CUVA and UCF-CAP with audit-guided captions.
NfCZJAaQdb.claimed_gains: Conditional joint usability spans 22.07% to 74.20% across the nine audited benchmarks under field-macro aggregation, and audit-guided caption fine-tuning on CUVA and UCF-CAP outperforms direct caption rewriting on VALU accuracy.

0ceSq2x2Ex.one_liner: Uses flow matching guided by quantized latent proximal interaction fields to reconstruct 3D human-object meshes from single RGB images.
0ceSq2x2Ex.problem: Single-image 3D human-object interaction reconstruction methods rely on sparse binary contact cues that miss continuous surface proximity and directional spatial coupling.
0ceSq2x2Ex.method: The authors represent dense surface-wide proximity and direction via InterFields, compress structured interaction patterns into a discrete quantized autoencoder manifold (LEXIS), and train LEXIS-Flow to jointly generate 3D human and object meshes with InterField-guided sampling.
0ceSq2x2Ex.key_idea: Encode dense surface proximity and direction in a quantized interaction manifold and jointly generate meshes and interaction fields via guided flow matching.
0ceSq2x2Ex.evidence: Evaluated on Open3DHOI and BEHAVE for 3D reconstruction, contact accuracy, physical plausibility, and cross-dataset generalization.

eMqhxx2vVv.one_liner: Analyzes how persistent versus layer-resampled additive, subtractive, and inactive edge roles interact with endpoint-dependent GNN message weights.
eMqhxx2vVv.problem: In stochastic graph message passing, it is unclear how persisting sampled edge roles across layers versus resampling them per layer alters adaptive endpoint-dependent weight averaging.
eMqhxx2vVv.method: Persistent Tri-State Message Passing (P3MP) pairs persistent additive, subtractive, and inactive edge roles with sample-specific endpoint weights and analytically decomposes two-layer preactivations into target-state feedback and weight-source covariance, validated via weight-vector permutations.
eMqhxx2vVv.key_idea: Combine persistent tri-state edge roles with endpoint-dependent weights and decompose two-layer preactivations into target-state feedback and weight-source covariance.
eMqhxx2vVv.evidence: Verified through two-layer theoretical derivations, exact enumeration, feature-only checkpoint measurements, and accuracy/loss comparisons of local versus shared weights on deduplicated Chameleon and Squirrel.

MgyYRvjASk.one_liner: Extracts authority claims from untrusted skill artifacts and gates sensitive agent tool calls against a trusted root.
MgyYRvjASk.problem: Skill-augmented LLM agents conflate untrusted workflow artifacts such as external skill files and tool outputs with execution authority, enabling forged approvals or policy claims to trigger unsafe tool actions.
MgyYRvjASk.method: SkillFence enforces execution authority separation by extracting authority claims from untrusted artifacts, estimating residual authority confusion, and gating every sensitive tool invocation against a trusted user or system policy root. The authors also construct an enterprise-style skill-context injection benchmark rewritten from 28 seed attacks.
MgyYRvjASk.key_idea: Separate informational context from execution authority by detecting artifact authority claims, estimating authority confusion, and verifying sensitive tool calls against trusted policy.
MgyYRvjASk.evidence: Evaluated on GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Kimi-2.5 agents across rewritten enterprise skill/tool attacks, benign utility tasks, and 500 transferred attacks.
MgyYRvjASk.claimed_gains: SkillFence cuts Broad ASR from 70.71% to 6.96%, 55.00% to 5.18%, and 41.16% to 2.86% across the three backbones while retaining 98.67%-100% benign utility and achieving 1.2%-1.8% Broad ASR on 500 transferred attacks.

w4h1cDcMpT.one_liner: Trains conditional flow-matching samplers of stationary turbulence by minimizing a self-consistent distributional-invariance residual from PDE dynamics.
w4h1cDcMpT.problem: Sampling statistically stationary turbulence typically requires costly long-time direct numerical simulation, while existing generative samplers either scale poorly with dimension or require pre-collected stationary samples.
w4h1cDcMpT.method: Invariant Measure Generator (IMG) formulates a self-consistent conditional flow-matching objective that turns the PDE distributional-invariance condition into a tractable training loss, optionally using targets produced by a frozen neural operator without solver calls during sampler training.
w4h1cDcMpT.key_idea: Convert the stationary invariant-measure condition of a dynamical system into a self-consistent conditional flow-matching loss without long-time simulation rollouts.
w4h1cDcMpT.evidence: Evaluated on Lorenz-63, the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation, and two-dimensional Hasegawa-Wakatani plasma turbulence including limited-data and frozen-neural-operator regimes.

76oHyMw1Pp.one_liner: Trajectory-robust visual-token admission preserves reusable, spatially covered evidence for efficient GUI agents.
76oHyMw1Pp.problem: Irreversible cache pruning can discard screenshot evidence needed for unknown future targets and cannot recover it without re-encoding.
76oHyMw1Pp.method: TRACE ranks evidence using a layout-derived interaction prior, instruction relevance, and feature novelty, while reserving native tokens for spatial coverage. Its nested token order supports monotonically shrinking budgets, and Monotone KV Contraction compacts retired frames into session state.
76oHyMw1Pp.key_idea: Create a nested evidence order with reserved spatial coverage so one cache-admission decision remains reusable across budgets and trajectory steps.
76oHyMw1Pp.evidence: No completed experiments are stated in the provided abstract.

YGYDXdejIb.one_liner: Observer-based state correction separates measurement assimilation from autonomous dynamics for time-series forecasting.
YGYDXdejIb.problem: Recurrent forecasters directly control latent dynamics with observations, causing a regime change when observations disappear at prediction time.
YGYDXdejIb.method: OSSMs treat inputs as measurements of an underlying autonomous system, using one transition across context and forecast intervals while observations correct state through an observer. The framework also recovers conventional and recent SSMs as particular instances.
YGYDXdejIb.key_idea: Propagate an autonomous latent state continuously and apply observation-based observer corrections only while measurements are available.
YGYDXdejIb.evidence: Experiments across several forecasting benchmarks compare OSSMs with corresponding SSM baselines at the same parameter count and training setup, alongside analysis of observability and estimation-error convergence.

7topH4JTgp.one_liner: Counterfactual video rollouts and relational rewards train language models to track relevant dynamics.
7topH4JTgp.problem: Video language models can answer correctly using static cues without responding to task-relevant spatiotemporal changes.
7topH4JTgp.method: CRPO constructs counterfactual videos through interventions such as horizontal flipping or temporal reversal and jointly optimizes factual and counterfactual rollouts. Relational supervision requires answers to change when relevant dynamics change and remain stable otherwise, without transformed-video labels.
7topH4JTgp.key_idea: Optimize relationships between paired factual and counterfactual responses according to whether an intervention changes the queried property.
7topH4JTgp.evidence: The paper introduces DyBench, a paired counterfactual benchmark for evaluating sensitivity to task-relevant video dynamics.

H1lbHZvBa7.one_liner: Moving-average gradients eliminate Newton-sketch statistical inefficiency without additional oracle evaluations.
H1lbHZvBa7.problem: Randomized sketching lowers Newton per-step computation but inflates the limiting covariance of last and averaged iterates.
H1lbHZvBa7.method: The method replaces each stochastic gradient in online sketched Newton optimization with a moving average. It analyzes the resulting last and averaged iterates while leaving the inner sketching solver's contraction bound unchanged.
H1lbHZvBa7.key_idea: Average gradients across steps to suppress sketch-induced statistical variance without changing oracle cost or solver contraction.
H1lbHZvBa7.evidence: Theory proves no covariance inflation for the last iterate relative to unaveraged gradients and minimax-optimal limiting covariance for the averaged iterate matching exact Newton.

KgsXW9XYqI.one_liner: Complementary random filters provide transferable reconstruction losses without pretrained features or manual weighting.
KgsXW9XYqI.problem: Pixel losses average away uncertain textures, while pretrained perceptual features are domain-specific and require task-specific engineering.
KgsXW9XYqI.method: RaFL compares predictions and targets through random convolutions, Fourier features, and wavelet filters, balancing them by gradient-norm matching. Design studies select filter families, resampling schedules, and initialization using validation PSNR and seed stability.
KgsXW9XYqI.key_idea: Match gradients across complementary randomly weighted filter families to automatically balance a domain-agnostic reconstruction loss.
KgsXW9XYqI.evidence: Evaluation covers three 2D and two 3D reconstruction tasks, five-task seed stability, and forward-FLOP comparisons with pixel and VGG19 perceptual losses.
KgsXW9XYqI.claimed_gains: RaFL outperforms a pixel loss on three tasks and matches it on two, adds less than 2% to backbone forward FLOPs, and requires 182× fewer loss FLOPs than a VGG19 perceptual loss.

7l5MbWjMzA.one_liner: Characterizes the exact-recovery information-theoretic learning boundary at window precision in forced-satisfiable planted k-SAT.
7l5MbWjMzA.problem: Exact recovery can succeed before observations uniquely determine a structured target, conflating recoverability with uniqueness.
7l5MbWjMzA.method: They analyze the version-space geometry of forced-satisfiable planted k-SAT in the scaling window, proving it forms a random subcube with Poisson-distributed unresolved coordinates.
7l5MbWjMzA.key_idea: Separates Bayes-optimal and minimax exact recovery from uniqueness via the random-subcube version-space geometry at window precision.
7l5MbWjMzA.evidence: Theoretical asymptotic analysis of forced-satisfiable planted k-SAT, including extensions to bounded non-uniform coordinate settings.
7l5MbWjMzA.claimed_gains: At m = n(2^k - 1)/k (ln n + x + o(1)) clauses, limiting uniqueness probability is exp(-e^-x) versus exp(-e^-x / 2) for exact recovery, requiring ln 2 (2^k - 1)n/k more clauses for uniqueness.

LiI0CpHJaJ.one_liner: Proposes World Critic Model (WCM), a LeJEPA-based history-conditioned critic combining return estimation with latent next-state prediction.
LiI0CpHJaJ.problem: Critics operating only on current observations miss temporal progress cues under partial observability, yet naively adding observation history fails to reliably improve VLA RL.
LiI0CpHJaJ.method: WCM encodes a short observation history and language instruction via a lightweight LeJEPA architecture into a shared temporal representation used to estimate returns and predict next-observation latents under executed actions.
LiI0CpHJaJ.key_idea: Jointly supervises a history-conditioned critic with return targets and action-conditioned latent next-observation prediction without pixel reconstruction.
LiI0CpHJaJ.evidence: Experiments across 149 tasks in four simulation benchmarks, ablations, and evaluations on seven real-world manipulation tasks across on-policy and off-policy RL and diverse VLA backbones.

R96nHYgceu.one_liner: Introduces RxnMiner, a multimodal agent with a chemistry toolbox, and ChemRxn-Bench for structured reaction extraction.
R96nHYgceu.problem: Extracting structured reaction records from chemistry figures is difficult because reactions are split across shared templates, substituent tables, and product grids.
R96nHYgceu.method: RxnMiner builds on Pi with an expert-informed extraction procedure and chemistry toolbox to recognize molecules, link shared and entry-specific evidence, and instantiate templates into source-linked records.
R96nHYgceu.key_idea: Coordinates multimodal molecular recognition, evidence association, and template instantiation using an agentic chemistry toolbox.
R96nHYgceu.evidence: Evaluated on ChemRxn-Bench (603 figures, 8,547 manually annotated reaction records) across five backbones including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
R96nHYgceu.claimed_gains: On ChemRxn-Bench, RxnMiner raises Qwen3.8-Flash-Next stereochemistry-aware reaction macro-F1 from 20.8% to 70.8%, compared with 25.0% for the strongest existing extraction baseline.

GZGMB6MWsQ.one_liner: Proposes 3D-GIA, associating unordered multi-view masks into scene-global identities to guide 3D Gaussian segmentation.
GZGMB6MWsQ.problem: Distilling view-dependent features or supervising 3D Gaussians with independently tracked masks causes inconsistent cross-view identities and semantic leakage across object boundaries.
GZGMB6MWsQ.method: 3D-GIA matches unordered hierarchical masks using 3D support, bidirectional reprojection, appearance, and cannot-links, then projects global clusters via confidence-weighted voting as soft targets for identity, language, and detached geometry fields.
GZGMB6MWsQ.key_idea: Clusters unordered multi-view masks with cannot-link constraints into scene-global identities projected onto Gaussians via confidence-weighted soft voting.
GZGMB6MWsQ.evidence: Evaluated on LERF-Mask and 3D-OVS, plus controlled common-mask comparisons against DEVA tracking and text-guided 3D editing tasks.
GZGMB6MWsQ.claimed_gains: Achieves 88.0% mIoU and 82.1% mBIoU on LERF-Mask and 96.2% mean mIoU on 3D-OVS.

Z7BQZUgzsZ.one_liner: Reduces variational inference for probabilistic time-series forecasting to multi-class classification in a fractionally differenced domain.
Z7BQZUgzsZ.problem: Probabilistic time-series forecasting must model complex, multimodal conditional distributions under distribution shift while staying computationally lightweight.
Z7BQZUgzsZ.method: The framework models outputs in a fractionally differenced domain using a finite mixture sieve and an analytically derived optimal reconstruction posterior. This reduces variational conditional distribution estimation to a multi-class classification objective with bounded logit gradients.
Z7BQZUgzsZ.key_idea: Operates in a fractionally differenced domain with a mixture sieve and analytical optimal posterior to cast variational forecasting as multi-class classification.
Z7BQZUgzsZ.evidence: Supported by quantization-level distributional approximation guarantees and experiments on real-world forecasting benchmarks.

XAvswNGHmG.one_liner: Evaluates mechanistic interpretability circuits separately on model successes and errors, showing circuits miss most errors.
XAvswNGHmG.problem: Circuit-based explanations validated by overall faithfulness closely reproduce a model's correct decisions while failing to explain its errors.
XAvswNGHmG.method: The authors measure exact answer agreement separately on model successes and failures across circuit sizes and ablation settings. They also test restoring omitted attention heads in an IOI case study to recover error reproduction.
XAvswNGHmG.key_idea: Stratifies circuit-faithfulness evaluation into exact agreement on model successes versus model errors across ablation regimes and circuit sizes.
XAvswNGHmG.evidence: Evaluated on IOI (GPT-2 small), Docstring, and six model-task settings from the Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark.
XAvswNGHmG.claimed_gains: On GPT-2 small IOI under mean ablation, tested circuits agree with 97.3–99.5% of correct prompts but only 11.4–41.7% of errors; restoring omitted heads raises error reproduction from 14.2% to 75.1%.

EICX2emBs8.one_liner: Uses coding agents offline to refine and compose modular visual tracking controllers around frozen visual backbones.
EICX2emBs8.problem: Visual trackers rely on manually designed online controller logic for search regions, response decoding, template memory, and recovery even as visual models advance.
EICX2emBs8.method: CRAFT tasks coding agents with proposing and testing offline controller revisions across four modular operations while keeping visual model weights fixed. A composing agent integrates selected mechanisms blindly, followed by joint refinement to produce standalone tracker code with no runtime LLM calls.
EICX2emBs8.key_idea: Decomposes tracker controller design into four operations for offline coding-agent search, blind composition, and joint refinement into standalone non-LLM code.
EICX2emBs8.evidence: Trained using the TNL2K training split as the sole source of tracking feedback.

AvkIUJ2ErG.one_liner: Generates self-verifying visual QA data via PixelProof using forward, rendering, and inverse image-processing Python programs.
AvkIUJ2ErG.problem: Constructing cheaply verifiable visual reasoning data without human supervision is difficult compared to math domains.
AvkIUJ2ErG.method: The authors propose PixelProof, where coding agents parameterize each visual question with a Forward program (scene spec to expected answer), a Renderer (scene to image), and an Inverse program (image-processing steps to independently verify the answer from pixels).
AvkIUJ2ErG.key_idea: Requiring agreement between a Forward scene-specification program and an Inverse pixel-processing program automatically verifies that visual QA answers are recoverable from rendered pixels.
AvkIUJ2ErG.evidence: Initial demonstration with five coding agents generating steered visual reasoning tasks.

TjI8o3WUbY.one_liner: Induces a single frozen semantic-relational conversation graph reused by sub-million-parameter readers across multiple safety tasks.
TjI8o3WUbY.problem: Multi-turn agentic safety tasks share dependence on accumulated conversational state but are typically trained and evaluated separately per task.
TjI8o3WUbY.method: A shared mention encoder and graph inducer extract persistent entity, action, goal, and constraint nodes with typed relations; this representation is frozen and consumed by three sub-million-parameter readers for jailbreak detection, action authorization, and topic segmentation.
TjI8o3WUbY.key_idea: Freezes a single induced semantic-relational conversation graph and pairs it with tiny task-specific readers to transfer across safety tasks and distribution shifts.
TjI8o3WUbY.evidence: Controlled transfer experiments across topic-matched jailbreak detection, InjecAgent action authorization, and dialogue topic segmentation.

u5zgxuaTtH.one_liner: Customizes LLM data synthesis and post-training around localized semantic error patterns in automated optimization modeling.
u5zgxuaTtH.problem: Post-training LLMs for automated optimization modeling suffers from sparse error-specific training examples and sparse rewards on hard problems.
u5zgxuaTtH.method: MIND exploits the observation that errors in optimization modeling often remain localized to specific semantic segments rather than propagating globally, tailoring data synthesis and post-training around these localizable error patterns.
u5zgxuaTtH.key_idea: Targets localized semantic-segment errors in optimization formulations to guide data synthesis and post-training supervision.
u5zgxuaTtH.evidence: Error-pattern profiling across problem-response pairs (further empirical details truncated in abstract).

kJkMIZHABv.one_liner: Adds scale-matched detached routing distributions from preceding MoE layers to current router logits before top-k dispatch.
kJkMIZHABv.problem: Standard Mixture-of-Experts routers ignore routing distributions computed by preceding layers despite cross-layer semantic dependencies.
kJkMIZHABv.method: HERO-MoE adds a residual branch of detached dense routing distributions from earlier MoE layers, scaled to match the current hidden representation magnitude and visible layer count, before softmax and top-k dispatch.
kJkMIZHABv.key_idea: Injects detached preceding-layer routing distributions via scale-preserving fusion into subsequent MoE routers without auxiliary losses or tuning parameters.
kJkMIZHABv.evidence: Pre-training experiments measuring training-loss reduction and end-to-end overhead with standard sparse dispatch.

O0FcFp5kqp.one_liner: Analyzes local-global indistinguishability in Planted Model RB via low-degree projections and tests GNN representation sensitivity.
O0FcFp5kqp.problem: Graph learners fail on global prediction tasks when local neighborhoods look identical across classes, and when GNNs can extract weak higher-order signals is unclear.
O0FcFp5kqp.method: Using Planted Model RB, the paper derives low-degree likelihood-ratio projections showing that pairwise shared-variable constraints carry the first informative signal, and compares GNNs with and without shared-variable graph representations.
O0FcFp5kqp.key_idea: Uses low-degree polynomial analysis on Planted Model RB to pinpoint shared-variable constraint pairs as the minimal local-global signal for GNNs.
O0FcFp5kqp.evidence: Low-degree theoretical bounds and GNN experiments varying problem size, constraint density, and graph representation.

d7nbCinzFp.one_liner: Measures video-language model memorization capacity in bits by compressing bindings between procedural videos and random strings.
d7nbCinzFp.problem: Existing multimodal memorization studies rely on similarity or extraction proxies without a common bit-level unit or capacity ceiling.
d7nbCinzFp.method: VidMem binds procedurally generated videos to independent random answer strings of known entropy and measures memorized information via conditional codelength reduction relative to a uniform reference.
d7nbCinzFp.key_idea: Quantifies video-language memorization in bits using conditional compression of procedural video-to-random-string associations.
d7nbCinzFp.evidence: Scaling experiments across decoder sizes, two decoder families, five frozen encoders, and continual-learning chunk-entropy ratios.
d7nbCinzFp.claimed_gains: Estimated capacity scales linearly at 2.54 bits per trained parameter in the calibration decoder family, and video-keyed associations require 1.28x as many parameters as text-keyed ones.

vIqJWgwSPu.one_liner: Pools ViT patches within Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher image regions into variable-length visual tokens for resolution-scalable VLMs.
vIqJWgwSPu.problem: Fixed spatial grid tokenization in VLMs causes visual token counts to scale with pixel area rather than scene content.
vIqJWgwSPu.method: RVLM partitions images with training-free Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher segmentation, pools ViT patches per region into variable-length visual tokens, and retains patch-to-region assignments for coarse-to-fine spatial decoding.
vIqJWgwSPu.key_idea: Replaces fixed spatial patch grids with region-pooled visual tokens derived from training-free Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher image segmentation.
vIqJWgwSPu.evidence: Evaluations across VQA, pointing, counting, segmentation, and depth estimation tasks against an identically trained patch baseline.
vIqJWgwSPu.claimed_gains: RVLM matches or improves task performance using 21.5% fewer visual tokens overall, and achieves a 5.3-point gain with 51.8% fewer visual tokens at the highest resolution.

9zyybbdlrv.one_liner: Selects pre-training checkpoints and data mixtures by weighting pre-training metrics—especially sampling lift—by correlation with post-training agentic outcomes.
9zyybbdlrv.problem: End-to-end training of small on-device agentic models is poorly understood because prior work isolates post-training or uses proprietary large-model recipes.
9zyybbdlrv.method: The authors show post-training sharpens behaviors already supported in pre-training and use sampling lift (multi-rollout gain over greedy decoding) plus correlation-weighted pre-training metrics to guide checkpoint selection and data-mixture allocation.
9zyybbdlrv.key_idea: Weights pre-training metrics including multi-rollout sampling lift by their correlation with post-training outcomes to guide checkpoint and data selection.
9zyybbdlrv.evidence: Empirical analysis relating pre-training behavioral diversity and metric correlations to downstream post-trained agentic performance.

olW2A6zx75.one_liner: Reconstructs 3D scenes from single images using coding agents that iteratively write, execute, render, and revise Blender programs.
olW2A6zx75.problem: Fixed 3D outputs or renderings from single images cannot be easily inspected, edited, or queried as explicit scene programs.
olW2A6zx75.method: LEGO-Anything frames single-image 3D reconstruction as an Image-to-Code loop in Blender, accompanied by LEGO-Bench (208 images from 104 indoor/outdoor scenes) and a training-free LEGO-Plugin addressing initialization, regressive edits, and self-evaluation.
olW2A6zx75.key_idea: Iteratively writes, executes, renders, and revises explicit Blender scene programs via a coding agent evaluated on simulator-grounded metrics.
olW2A6zx75.evidence: Evaluated coding agents on LEGO-Bench across artifact validity, visible-surface geometry, and rendered appearance, plus trajectory failure analysis.
olW2A6zx75.claimed_gains: Across evaluated coding agents on LEGO-Bench, GPT-6-astra achieves 53.4% indoor and 39.6% outdoor scores.

65nUb5ZxbN.one_liner: Replaces Gaussian priors in flow matching with a noised low-frequency image projection so identity coupling is OT-optimal.
65nUb5ZxbN.problem: Computing optimal transport couplings between Gaussian priors and data is cubic in sample count, forcing costly or biased approximations.
65nUb5ZxbN.method: The authors design the prior as a low-frequency projection of natural images interpolated with Gaussian noise, sampled at inference by a lightweight model, making the identity coupling OT-optimal without modifying the flow model.
65nUb5ZxbN.key_idea: Uses a Gaussian-noised low-frequency image projection as the flow-matching prior so the identity coupling is optimal-transport optimal.
65nUb5ZxbN.evidence: Evaluated in latent-space flow matching, classifier-free guidance, and one-step generation settings.
65nUb5ZxbN.claimed_gains: Reduces trajectory curvature by more than 2x relative to standard priors.

PtaGpoa0gf.one_liner: Achieves order-optimal regret and budget violation in constrained online convex optimization with noisy, correlated constraint observations.
PtaGpoa0gf.problem: Online convex optimization with time-varying constraints lacks tight guarantees when constraint values are observed only through correlated, bounded-variance noise.
PtaGpoa0gf.method: The LEDGER algorithm takes one projection per round without requiring a strictly feasible action, using unbiased estimates of the loss gradient, constraint gradient, and noisy constraint value. The authors prove upper bounds on expected regret and interval budget violation alongside matching Gaussian-noise lower bounds.
PtaGpoa0gf.key_idea: Uses a single-projection online update from noisy loss/constraint gradients and noisy constraint values to match information-theoretic regret and budget-violation bounds.
PtaGpoa0gf.evidence: Theoretical upper bounds on expected regret and budget violation plus matching minimax lower bounds under Gaussian constraint noise.
PtaGpoa0gf.claimed_gains: LEDGER achieves O(sqrt(T)) expected regret and O(sqrt(T log(eT))) expected budget violation over T rounds, matching a lower bound of order sqrt(T log T).

HkHm2LAXXA.one_liner: Establishes the first gap-dependent regret bound for LSVI-UCB++ and matching lower bounds for linear MDPs.
HkHm2LAXXA.problem: Prior gap-dependent regret analyses for linear MDPs do not apply to nearly minimax-optimal algorithms like LSVI-UCB++ and leave leading dimension/horizon tightness open.
HkHm2LAXXA.method: The authors prove a gap-dependent expected regret upper bound for LSVI-UCB++, a structural lower bound for persistent ellipsoidal optimism algorithms, and two general algorithm-independent lower bounds for linear MDPs. Together these characterize the intrinsic quadratic feature-dimension and cubic horizon dependence.
HkHm2LAXXA.key_idea: Derives a gap-dependent upper bound for LSVI-UCB++ and matching lower bounds for persistent ellipsoidal optimism and general linear MDP learners.
HkHm2LAXXA.evidence: Purely theoretical proofs of upper and lower gap-dependent regret bounds in linear MDPs.
HkHm2LAXXA.claimed_gains: Proves an expected regret upper bound of O_tilde(d^2 H^3 / Delta_min + d^6 H^5) for LSVI-UCB++ and a matching lower bound of Omega(d^2 H^3 / Delta_min).

LZ615nsmDF.one_liner: Represents multi-agent harnesses as dynamic graphs and learns an online graph-edit policy via global GRPO and local perturbation feedback.
LZ615nsmDF.problem: Multi-agent system harnesses (prompts, tools, memory, control flow) are tightly coupled and require dynamic runtime adaptation under delayed task-level feedback.
LZ615nsmDF.method: G-Harness unifies multi-agent execution state and harness structure as a dynamic graph and trains a task-conditioned graph-edit policy to construct and rewrite harnesses online. It optimizes the policy with a global-local framework combining global GRPO task utility with local graph-perturbation credit assignment.
LZ615nsmDF.key_idea: Models multi-agent execution and configuration as a dynamic graph rewritten online by an RL graph-edit policy trained with global GRPO and local perturbation feedback.

mLUAHA3mLf.one_liner: Coordinates multitask differentiable quality-diversity search using subspace-projected repulsion and adaptive inter-task transfer.
mLUAHA3mLf.problem: Solving multiple related quality-diversity tasks independently causes redundant exploration and missed opportunities to reuse transferable solutions.
mLUAHA3mLf.method: MTQD-CoD jointly optimizes related QD tasks using subspace-projected repulsion to steer task-specific searchers into less-overlapping regions and adapts cross-task transfer probabilities based on observed archive contributions.
mLUAHA3mLf.key_idea: Combines subspace-projected inter-task repulsion with archive-contribution-weighted transfer probability adaptation across multitask QD searchers.
mLUAHA3mLf.evidence: Evaluated on arm repertoire, latent-space illumination, and policy optimization problems.

a7Rw7sWq9e.one_liner: Optimizes adversarial audio perturbations with a two-phase token-weighted loss and selects candidates by execution outcomes.
a7Rw7sWq9e.problem: Teacher-forced response loss can guide adversarial audio optimization without reliably ranking freely generated tool calls from voice agents.
a7Rw7sWq9e.method: ActionWhisper optimizes a bounded speech-difference perturbation using distinct weights on call-format, tool-name, and argument tokens across a two-phase schedule. Periodically, it decodes without target prefixes and selects candidates using parser/executor outcomes, breaking ties with response loss.
a7Rw7sWq9e.key_idea: Combines two-phase token-weighted teacher-forced loss for waveform search with prefix-free decoding and execution-grounded candidate selection.
a7Rw7sWq9e.evidence: Evaluated across four Audio LLMs and two agent frameworks on 120 executable cases.
a7Rw7sWq9e.claimed_gains: Reaches 28.3% macro-average precise-action rate across 120 cases, compared with 22.0% for Target-Text CE.

hQQJxWrEru.one_liner: Trains LLMs with RL across sequential iterations and parallel asynchronous trajectories inside a minimal shared-memory discovery loop.
hQQJxWrEru.problem: LLMs in scientific discovery suffer from narrow exploration and premature convergence, while evolutionary harnesses rely on rigid manual heuristics.
hQQJxWrEru.method: Loop RL pairs a minimal loop harness—offering only sequential iteration, parallel execution, and asynchronous shared memory—with reinforcement learning that assigns credit across both iterations and parallel trajectories.
hQQJxWrEru.key_idea: Assigns RL credit across sequential iterations and parallel trajectories inside a minimal asynchronous shared-memory loop harness without hardcoded search heuristics.
hQQJxWrEru.evidence: Evaluated on scientific discovery tasks (exact benchmarks not detailed in abstract snippet).

uvr0FPNMyf.one_liner: Matched fresh-session sequences isolate how retained experience changes later personal-agent task performance.
uvr0FPNMyf.problem: Personal agents retain memories, skills, and histories without controlled evidence that retained experience improves later behavior through intended pathways.
uvr0FPNMyf.method: PAST-Bench runs ordered fresh-session tasks with retained experience switched on and off under matched conditions and tracks save, retrieve, and update pathways. Hermes+ adds five targeted interventions to Hermes, one per agent-loop stage.
uvr0FPNMyf.key_idea: Measure later-task gains under matched retention conditions and attribute them to evidence of the intended memory pathway.
uvr0FPNMyf.evidence: The benchmark spans 26 scenarios and 204 episodes across seven base models and four agent frameworks, followed by diagnostic interventions in Hermes+.
uvr0FPNMyf.claimed_gains: The full Hermes+ system doubles the gain on tasks requiring outdated-state replacement but regresses on procedural reuse.

YktbTmReXm.one_liner: Maintains two-timescale global and local latent distributions updated from numerical residuals to guide LM symbolic equation discovery.
YktbTmReXm.problem: Language-model equation discovery methods pass feedback via example programs or text memory without separating persistent structural preferences from fast local residual corrections.
